Position Overview
We're hiring a Security Engineer to own the security posture of our platform and production workloads. This is a hands-on engineering role sitting at the intersection of architecture, engineering and security. You’ll make sure security is designed into systems rather than bolted on afterwards, test whether our security assumptions and controls actually work, and help teams build systems that remain secure and resilient when things go wrong. Your role will include running offensive testing against our own infrastructure.
A significant part of the role is securing how we build and ship AI products. As teams move faster with AI-assisted development, you'll define the sandboxing, isolation, permissions and guardrail patterns that let that happen safely, and tune them as the tooling and threat landscape change.
You'll work in close partnership with Engineering and our AI practice, embedded in design reviews and delivery work rather than reviewing from the outside. Our IT function leads compliance administration, you’ll provide the engineering expertise and technical controls needed to support SOC 2, GDPR and PCI DSS obligations. We value evidence over assumptions - we want to know whether security measures work in practice, not simply whether they exist.
What you will be doing:
* Own the engineering implementation and continuous improvement of security controls supporting SOC 2 Type II, working with IT on evidence collection and external audits
* Act as the security partner in architecture and design reviews, setting secure-by-default patterns for new services, data flows, and integrations, while making pragmatic trade-offs between risk and delivery
* Design, propose, and tune sandboxing and isolation models for AI-assisted and AI-generated code, including execution boundaries, secrets handling, permissions, dependency controls, and output validation
* Own our offensive security testing, combining internal application, cloud and infrastructure testing with third-party penetration testing where useful; test whether important security assumptions actually hold, and verify remediation
* Maintain and extend our GDPR and PCI DSS control posture, working with Legal, Finance, and Engineering on data mapping, retention, cardholder-data scope, and DPIAs
* Work with Platform Engineering to tune security tooling and automation across the SDLC: SAST, DAST, dependency and container scanning, IaC policy checks, and CI/CD gates - focussing on high-signal, actionable checks and removing controls or gates that create friction without materially reducing risk
* Lead threat modelling for high-risk services and AI features, and translate findings into prioritised, actionable engineering work
* Work with Engineering to improve detection and response capability: logging coverage, alerting quality, runbooks, and participation in incident response
* Support customer and prospect security reviews, questionnaires, and due diligence with accurate, evidence-backed responses
* Raise the security baseline across engineering through guidance, tooling, and enablement rather than gatekeeping
What we are looking for
Must have:
* 5+ years in a security engineering, application security, or cloud security role, with meaningful time spent hands-on rather than purely advisory
* Direct experience operating or contributing to SOC 2 Type II controls in a live environment, not just preparing for an initial audit, but sustaining and evidencing controls over time
* Practical penetration testing skills: web application, API, and cloud infrastructure testing, with the ability to run assessments internally and validate third-party findings
* Strong cloud security background (AWS): IAM design, network segmentation, encryption, secrets management, and workload isolation
* Working knowledge of PCI DSS requirements and how to scope, segment, and evidence a cardholder-data environment
* Solid grasp of GDPR as it applies to engineering: lawful basis, data minimisation, retention, subject rights, cross-border transfers, and sub-processor management
* Secure architecture and threat modelling experience across distributed, service-based systems
* Strong hands-on engineering ability: able to read and reason about application code, write scripts and automation, and integrate security checks into CI/CD
* Experience securing containerised workloads and infrastructure-as-code (Kubernetes, OpenTofu, or equivalents)
* Ability to influence engineers and product teams without authority, make pragmatic risk trade-offs rather than absolutist ones, and challenge security controls that create cost or friction without proportionate benefit
* Clear written communication: you'll be producing control documentation, findings, and customer-facing security responses
* Experience securing AI/LLM systems: prompt injection, tool-use and agent permissions, model and data exfiltration risks, RAG pipeline security, and evaluation of AI-generated code
Good to have:
* Exposure to ISO 27001, or experience running a multi-framework compliance programme
* Offensive security certifications (OSCP, OSWE, GWAPT) or equivalent demonstrable experience
* Detection engineering and SIEM experience, including writing and tuning detections
* Familiarity with AI security frameworks such as the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, NIST AI RMF, or ISO/IEC 42001
* Experience in a high-growth SaaS environment, particularly one handling sensitive personal data at scale
* Background in EdTech, or experience with sector-specific requirements such as accessibility, student data privacy (FERPA), or institutional procurement security reviews
* Experience using controlled security experiments, incident simulations, chaos engineering, or similar techniques to test how systems behave when assumptions or safeguards fail
* Prior involvement in incident response for a real production incident, including post-incident review
Benefits
Our benefits are all aimed at supporting a healthy work-life balance and cultivating a company culture where you can bring your whole, human self to work.
Here's what we offer:
* 🌴 35 days holiday per year (excluding public holidays!) - yep, that’s not a typo!

* ❤️ Enhanced maternity & paternity allowance

job_description:
Block is one company built from many blocks, all united by the same purpose: economic empowerment. We build technology that increases access and independence for sellers, individuals, and artists around the world. Working at Block means working on and across our brands—Square, Cash App, Afterpay, TIDAL, Spiral, and Proto— in roles that connect, enable, and push all of them forward faster.

As Global Fulfillment Operations Specialist at Block, you’ll drive reliable day-to-day fulfillment of hardware across our global brands and markets. You’ll work through third-party logistics providers (3PLs) and alongside regional supplier managers to keep orders moving, resolve operational exceptions, improve inventory and shipment visibility, and strengthen the processes that connect our systems and fulfillment partners.
This individual contributor role combines hands-on operational execution, analytical problem-solving, and continuous improvement. You’ll independently own fulfillment outcomes, turning recurring issues into durable controls and scalable processes rather than repeated manual work.
## **Key Responsibilities**
**Global Fulfillment Execution & Partner Performance**
* Own fulfillment outcomes from order release through shipment confirmation for customer orders, replacements, inventory transfers, and other fulfillment flows.
* Monitor order accuracy, processing timeliness, backlog, holds, and shipment exceptions; coordinate recovery and prioritize work within established business guidelines.
* Drive outcomes through 3PL partners, ensuring they own their commitments rather than transferring recurring work to Block.
* Partner with regional supplier managers on service expectations, performance reviews, capacity risks, and operational improvements.
* Maintain clear escalation paths and cross-time-zone handoffs; support continuity and recovery during disruptions.
* Manage actionable reporting on fulfillment performance, exceptions, and corrective actions; use data to prioritize and measure improvements.
**Systems, Inventory & Operational Controls**
* Investigate order, inventory, and shipment discrepancies across systems.
* Coordinate inventory reconciliation and resolution of interface failures, missing transactions, configuration errors, and data issues with the appropriate owners.
* Validate system and process changes before and after implementation.
* Maintain warehouse procedures and controls that ensure accurate execution, traceability, and reliable handoffs.
**Continuous Improvement & Launch Readiness**
* Identify recurring failures and manual work; eliminate, automate, or simplify them through root-cause improvements.
* Independently lead defined improvement initiatives through implementation and measured results.
* Build standard work, self-service resources, and exception-management processes that reduce individual intervention.
* Enable product launches, new markets and channels, and warehouse or system transitions by testing fulfillment flows and closing readiness gaps.
**Supplier Cost Management & Billing Controls**
* Validate fulfillment supplier invoices against contracted rates, actual activity, and approved charges; resolve discrepancies and track credits through closure.
* Monitor spend and cost per order, investigate variances, and identify savings opportunities without compromising service.
* Partner with supplier managers and Finance to improve billing accuracy, cost reporting, and automated controls that prevent recurring errors.
## **Qualifications**
### **Required Experience & Skills**
* 5+ years of relevant experience in fulfillment, order management, warehouse operations, logistics, or supply chain, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
* Practical knowledge of ERP, order-management, and warehouse-management systems, including investigating transaction and inventory discrepancies.
* Strong analytical skills and proficiency with driving controls through operational reporting.
* Demonstrated ability to independently manage operational workflows, resolve exceptions, and deliver defined improvement projects.
* Ability to identify root causes and build repeatable solutions rather than rely on recurring manual intervention
* Ability to influence internal stakeholders and external partners without direct authority.

# Senior Public Affairs & Statutory Partnerships Manager
**About Bloomsbury Football Foundation**
In 2018, Bloomsbury Football Foundation started with four kids and a bag of footballs on a housing estate in Camden. Today, we reach over 7,000 children and young people every week across London and we're just getting started.
We exist because not every child grows up with the same opportunities to play, belong, and progress. Too many young people are locked out of the game by cost, circumstance, or geography. We're changing that and using football, the world's most popular sport, as a powerful vehicle for health, wellbeing, and social change. It's not about producing stars. It's about shaping better futures.
In just a few years, our income has grown from £1m to over £5m. We're now expanding beyond London into areas of deprivation across the country, with ambitions to reach over 40,000 young people every week by 2031. No other sport-for-good charity in the UK has achieved scale at this level. We intend to be the first.
To get there, we need people who believe what we believe that football has the unique power to change lives. Forward, together.
**Our commitment to inclusion**
At Bloomsbury, belonging isn't just something we create for the young people we serve it's something we live as an organisation and is embedded into core values. We are committed to building a team that reflects the communities we work in, and we actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds, ethnicities, and identities.
We particularly welcome applications from women and people from underrepresented groups, who remain underrepresented in both the sport and charity sectors. We know that the best idea wins regardless of who it comes from, and we are proud to be building an organisation where everyone has a place to play, belong, and progress.
**About the role**
We are creating a public affairs function at Bloomsbury Football Foundation, and we are looking for the person to build and lead it. You will own our relationship with government and the wider statutory world at the moment it matters most: as we scale from a London charity into a national one, growing towards 40,000 young people a week across five cities by 2030.
The rationale is straightforward. Government is the largest single institutional funder of charities in the UK, and that funding concentrates overwhelmingly in larger organisations, the £10m-plus band Bloomsbury is heading towards. It flows through many channels: open grant rounds, but also commissioned contracts and tenders run by councils, the NHS and national programmes, and the funds of regulatory and quasi-governmental bodies. And the challenges we address, from inactivity and poor mental health to youth violence and social mobility, are among the biggest this country faces, which is why what we do commands serious political attention. Your job is to convert that into income: to build the relationships, shape the propositions, and win the funding that takes our work national.
This is a commercial target as much as a political one. By 2030, at national scale, we want statutory sources to make up 25-30% of our revenue, in the region of £6-7m a year. You would own that goal.
Crucially, you would not do it from a proposition we wait to be asked for. Much of this role is proactive: creating compelling, fundable propositions and taking them to ministers, officials and commissioners, not only being front of mind when an application window opens. It also runs well beyond the point of award: you would own many of our statutory funder relationships for the long term, through reporting and stewardship, roundtables and events, and bringing officials and ministers to see our delivery on the ground.
One of the things that makes this role rare is the platform behind it. Bloomsbury has strong links into 10 Downing Street and some of the most senior people in government, access very few charities of our size can offer. You would be building on existing relationships, not starting cold.
The role sits within our fundraising team, led by our Director of Fundraising, alongside colleagues in trusts and foundations, corporate partnerships, philanthropy, events and fundraising operations. It is not a silo. The same people and institutions move between these worlds: major philanthropists back political parties and attend the same roundtables; large institutional grant-makers increasingly co-fund with government or take a funder-plus approach that includes political engagement. So this role both feeds and benefits from the wider pipeline. You would work particularly closely with our Senior Trusts Lead, who is already involved in our public affairs work and will remain a key collaborator, and with our fundraising operations colleagues to build a systematised sales funnel across statutory and institutional income.
**About you — what we're looking for**You are a serious operator in the political world, with the network, the judgement and the instinct for opportunity that only real experience brings. But you are more than a skilled political operator: you are commercially minded, a first-rate relationship-builder and closer who is energised by the pursuit of significant income and holds yourself accountable for the numbers. You are equally comfortable holding a conversation with a minister and writing a winning seven-figure bid. You are also a warm and popular presence inside a team, not only outside it, the kind of colleague others want to work with and bring into the room. You are ambitious, for your own career and for what Bloomsbury can become, and you are excited by the rare chance to build a function that will be critical to the charity's growth and, ultimately, the life chances of tens of thousands of young people. *Please note: This role is subject to safer recruitment measures, including a satisfactory Enhanced Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check and a public-domain social media/online background check in compliance with current data protection guidelines.*
## Key Responsibilities
**Relationship and political engagement**
* Build and maintain Bloomsbury's relationships across the statutory ecosystem: government departments, ministers and their offices, Parliament, the civil service, local authorities, and the regulatory and quasi-governmental bodies that fund and shape our work, so we are known and trusted where decisions are made.
* Engage across the political spectrum on a strictly cross-party, apolitical basis, working with whoever is in government and building relationships that outlast any single administration.
* Network relentlessly on Bloomsbury's behalf, representing the charity with credibility and warmth to the most senior political and official audiences.
* Track the policy landscape across youth, sport, community, education and social mobility, spotting opportunities and risks early and briefing leadership on what matters and why.
* Represent Bloomsbury at political events, party conferences, roundtables and sector forums, and create opportunities for our CEO and leadership to do the same.
**Winning statutory income**
* Own our pipeline of government and statutory funding, from horizon-scanning to award, across grants, commissioned contracts and competitive tenders.
* Create proactive, fundable propositions to take to ministers, officials and commissioners, rather than waiting for open application rounds.
* Lead the writing of bids and tenders to an exceptional standard: evidence-led, commercially sharp, and competitive with the best in the sector.
* Develop and contribute to consortia and partnership bids, working with councils, other charities and local partners, as this is increasingly the route to the largest funds.
* Oversee relationships and grants with quasi-governmental and regulatory funders such as the Youth Endowment Fund, Sport England and FIFA.
* Work closely with the programmes and finance teams to ensure every bid is deliverable as well as fundable, and that Bloomsbury is bid-ready when major rounds open.
**Stewardship, profile and leadership**
* Own statutory funder relationships after the award: reporting, stewardship, roundtables, events, and bringing officials and ministers to see delivery on the ground.
* Work with our marketing and communications team to build Bloomsbury's political profile, securing the right PR, coverage and presence to support our funding and influence goals.
* Work with fundraising operations colleagues to build a systematised sales funnel across statutory and institutional income.
* Turn our impact evidence into a compelling political narrative that lands with policymakers and funders.
* Lead Bloomsbury's public affairs function from the outset, shaping its strategy and priorities, and building a team beneath you as we scale.
## Skills, Knowledge and Expertise
**Essential criteria**
* Significant experience in the political world: a minimum of five years across government, Parliament, a political party, public affairs, policy or a closely related field
* A strong, active network across the statutory ecosystem, and a proven ability to build new relationships at senior level
* A track record of securing statutory, political or institutional income, through grants, commissioned contracts or competitive tenders, or of writing high-quality, winning bids
* A commercial, target-driven mindset, with the drive and appetite to bring in significant income
* Excellent written communication, with the ability to turn evidence into a persuasive political and funding narrative
* Sound political judgement and discretion, with the maturity to represent the organisation credibly at the most senior levels, and the ability to work on a strictly cross-party, apolitical basis
* A proactive, ownership mindset: you build things, take initiative, and follow through without being chased
* The ability to stay sharp and effective across many priorities in a fast-paced, growing organisation
* Strong alignment with BFF's values and a genuine belief in football as a tool for social impact
* Eligibility to live and work in the UK

* Direct experience of the youth, sport, education or social mobility policy landscape
* Experience of government commissioning, contracts and tenders, from either side of the table
* Experience developing or leading consortia and partnership bids
* Experience building or leading a public affairs or policy function, rather than only operating within one
* An existing network within relevant government departments, select committees, arms-length bodies or funders such as the Youth Endowment Fund
* Experience line-managing or growing a team

* Opportunities to attend Premier League, WSL, FA Cup, League Cup, and Champions League matches

# Senior Database Engineer
London
**We’re Capital on Tap 👋**💳 Capital on Tap started because small businesses were underserved. Big banks were slow, their products weren't fit for purpose, and small business owners often couldn't access what they needed. We set out to fix that.
Today we're a financial platform - not just a credit card company. We offer a best-in-class business credit card, SME-focused spend management platform, a savings product that hit £1 billion in funds within its first year, and a growing suite of tools and financial products that make running a small business easier. 1,000+ employees, £20bn in annual card spend, 200,000+ customers, 17,000+ Trustpilot reviews averaging 4.7 stars, and we're profitable. We’ve done a pretty good job so far, but we’re just getting started!
📍London, Old Street | 🏢 2 Days in Office
**Database Engineering at Capital on Tap 🌞**
Our platform runs on .NET and SQL Server on Azure, and it has grown a long way past what it was originally designed for. We are hiring our first dedicated database performance engineer to own performance and scale: to make the fast paths fast, to keep them fast as volume grows, and to give every engineer here the tooling and the judgement to write data access that holds up in production. You will join a small agile team comprising DBAs and site reliability engineers in a hands-on senior individual contributor role. You will not be a ticket queue. You will pick the work that moves latency, cost and reliability, and you will be trusted to say what needs re-architecting.
**What You'll Do**
* Own query and index performance across our transactional SQL Server estate, using execution plans, Query Store, wait statistics, real production telemetry or other data driven measures.
* Investigate and implement horizontal scaling techniques such as multi-cluster architecture, contained availability groups, sharding, etc, to ensure Capital on Tap’s distributed software estate can continue to support a fast growing customer base and increasing service count.
* Find and remove the bottlenecks on our latency critical paths, starting with card authorisation and ledger read/writes, and hold them to an agreed p99 budget.
* Own high availability and disaster recovery. Availability groups, failover, backup and restore testing against real RTO and RPO targets, and the runbooks that go with them.
* Build and enhance self serve tooling to enable development teams to identify query plan regressions along with self service diagnostic tools to allow teams to debug their own query performance.
* Automate what is currently manual, using PowerShell, Python, or Terraform, and treat database configuration as code.
* Manage SQL Server cost as a first-class metric alongside latency and uptime.
* Work alongside Product Engineering and our data analytics team, reviewing designs before they ship and levelling up how the whole engineering org thinks about data access.
**Our Values & Culture**
* **Just Pilot:** We never settle for “good enough”. We pilot new ideas fast, ask questions to figure it out, and scale quickly.
* **Why Not Today?** Fast is as slow as we go - speed and simplicity gives us a competitive advantage.
* **Be a Buddy:** We tap in from day one to help the team, we do the right thing even if it’s hard.
* **Owners and Dates:** We don’t chase people. If you own a task and agree to a date, the expectation is that it gets done.
* **Feedback:** We want our employees to flourish, so we regularly provide direct and constructive feedback.
**What We're Looking For 🔎**
* Substantial experience running Microsoft SQL Server in production at scale, whether that be self managed, Managed Instances, or on Azure SQL, in a business where downtime and latency have direct commercial impact.
* Real depth in the internals. The query optimiser and plan cache, indexing and statistics, locking, blocking and isolation levels, tempdb, and the wait types that tell you which of those is actually hurting you.
* A track record of specific, measurable performance wins you can walk us through end to end.
* Experience scaling relational data past the point where tuning alone works. Partitioning, archival, denormalisation, caching, read replicas, or a considered move to a different store.
* Comfortable writing application code, not just scripts. T-SQL to an expert level, plus PowerShell or Python, and infrastructure as code.
* Hands-on with HA/DR design and with leading production incidents.
* Experience working with ORMs (ideally Entity Framework) and the particular performance tradeoffs that come with an ORM.
* Working knowledge of other database engines such as PostgreSQL, and views on the relative pros/cons.
* An ability to translate technical concepts and tradeoffs to non-database specialists.

* 45 minute tech chat with Hiring Manager
* 90 minute technical interview
* 30 minute values interview with Head of Platform Engineering

# R&D Engineer (Thermodynamics)

## Description
Our journey from start-up to global leader in industrial Carbon Capture
Carbon Clean has been developing and providing carbon capture solutions since around 2009. Over the years, we have grown our expertise and technology, including the Cyclone CC system, to help industries reduce carbon emissions more efficiently. In the next phase of our growth, we are seeking an impactful **R&D Engineer (Thermodynamics).**
| London, UK | | Competitive + Incentive Awards tied to your performance + Benefits
**The Role**
The Engineering & Process Research (E&PR) team drives process innovation at Carbon Clean, solving high-value problems and filling critical knowledge gaps. As an R&D Engineer (Thermodynamics), you will build custom property, VLE and reaction models for advanced solvent formulations, maintain and improve existing solvent models, incorporate novel reaction schemes, and drive the advancement of Carbon Clean's solvent formulations through a range of simulation practices.
You will be an expert in thermodynamics and accomplished in the numerical implementation of solvers and optimisers for model regression. Working directly with wet-lab specialists, you will help propose and design experiments, contribute to idea generation and intellectual property, and consult with internal and external stakeholders on well-communicated, tailored solutions.
Reporting to the Engineering and Process Research Manager within E&PR. Full-time, 37.5 hours a week.
**What success looks like:**
· Robust, validated solvent models (thermo-kinetic, property and thermal degradation) that measurably improve prediction accuracy against lab data.
· Accurate activity coefficient models in place for Carbon Clean's novel solvent formulations.
· Experimental programmes co-designed with wet-lab teams that close the key data gaps for model validation.
· New modelling approaches and reaction schemes that contribute to process innovation and intellectual property.
· Clear, regular communication of results that stakeholders trust and act on.
## Requirements
**Role Focus:**
· **50-60%:** Solvent thermodynamic and kinetic model development, including activity coefficient (eNRTL), VLE, property and degradation models, and large-scale parameter regression.
· **25-30%:** Experimental collaboration and model validation, including co-designing experiments, simulation planning and data analysis.
· **10-20%:** Innovation and communication, including literature review, novel reaction schemes, IP generation, and reporting to internal and external stakeholders.
**Responsibilities consist of but not limited to...**
**Solvent Modelling & Thermodynamics**
· Build and own the development of solvent models, including thermo-kinetic, property and thermal degradation models.
· Validate models using lab data and continuously refine them to improve predictions.
· Be able to accurately interpret experimental data, engage with experimentalists to improve data quality, and identify datasets needed to build and improve models.
· Drive the building of accurate activity coefficient models for novel solvent formulations, identifying the best approaches and proactively overcoming technical challenges.
· Implement solvers and optimisers to regress large-parameter models against experimental data.
**Experimental Collaboration & Model Validation**
· Collaborate with experimental teams to design experiments and specify datasets and studies that support model validation and improvement.
· Proactively prepare simulation plans in support of project goals.
· Perform post-processing and data analysis using your knowledge of reaction engineering and thermodynamics.
**Innovation & Continuous Improvement**
· Keep up with the literature and apply novel approaches and reaction schemes to improve model fidelity and predictive capability.
· Play an integral part in idea generation, driving process innovation and intellectual property generation for Carbon Clean.
**Communication & Stakeholder Engagement**
· Prepare figures, reports and presentations documenting project results.
· Present results regularly to internal and external stakeholders.
· Engage proactively with stakeholders, offering thoughtful, well-communicated solutions tailored to their requirements.
**You are an ideal candidate if...**
· You hold a Ph.D. in Chemical Engineering or a related discipline with relevant thesis work, plus at least 2 years of relevant research experience in an industrial setting (3-4 years preferred).
· You have built thermo-kinetic models for multi-component polar, non-ideal mixtures, ideally in CO[2] capture or gas treating applications.
· You have 2+ years' experience in solution thermodynamics modelling of non-ideal, polar, reactive mixtures using gamma-phi approaches with Electrolyte NRTL (preferred) or SAFT.
· You have built, solved and optimised robust kinetic models that incorporate fundamental process chemistry.
· You have used off-the-shelf optimisers (e.g. HEEDS, SciPy, Pyomo) to fit large-parameter models (100+ parameters) to experimental data.
· You are proficient in Python and process simulation software such as AVEVA Process Simulation, Aspen Plus, gPROMS or similar.
· You have led projects and provided technical mentoring in an industrial R&D setting.
· You are comfortable working with a global team across UK, US and India time zones.
· You are self-motivated and self-reliant, with excellent written and verbal communication and problem-solving skills.
**The application journey has 4 key steps**
1. Recruiter call (initial 30 mins conversation)
2. Technical interview with the Hiring Manager
3. Technical case study or presentation with the E&PR team
4. Final interview with senior leadership
*This process should take around 3-4 weeks - your schedule is really important to us, so we promise to be as flexible as possible!*
Join a mission-driven team tackling one of the world's toughest challenges: decarbonising heavy industry, with an ambition to capture 1 billion tonnes of CO[2]. In this role, your models will directly shape the next generation of Carbon Clean's solvent technology and contribute to new intellectual property, working alongside experimental specialists across the UK, US and India.
## Benefits
**In addition, we offer you:**
· The opportunity to continue to develop both personally and professionally, in our rapidly growing company.
· A culture that encourages excellence, ownership, flexibility and care.
· Our great workplaces with excellent facilities and perks, where we can come together to collaborate with like-minded colleagues.

**We provide these benefits & perks:**

**We believe everyone Belongs @ Carbon Clean**
We are passionate and committed to our people. At Carbon Clean, you will be working in an inclusive environment where everyone belongs. # eDiscovery Project Manager
The eDiscovery Project Manager will play a key role within the Firm’s Data Privacy and eDiscovery function, supporting the efficient management of electronic discovery processes, data subject rights requests, and related compliance activities.
Reporting to the Data Privacy Officer (DPO), the eDiscovery Project Manager will work with the eDiscovery Manager by providing technical support, predominantly on file reviews, transfers and data subject access requests (DSARs), as part of the Firm’s in-house compliance and regulatory requirements. In addition, the eDiscovery Project Manager may be required to assist fee-earning teams, such as Employment, Litigation and Dispute Resolution, with eDiscovery for disputes and claims. The ideal candidate will possess knowledge of litigation, DSARs and file transfer processes, document management and access to data and data organisation, have a broad range of experience in applied technology and be able to make recommendations to improve our practices and implement the best technical and practical solutions.
**Roles and Responsibilities**
* Manage end-to-end eDiscovery projects across the firm, including scoping, data collection, processing, review, and production for both internal compliance matters and fee earner client work.
* Partner with fee-earning teams across practice areas including Litigation, Employment, Dispute Resolution, and Corporate to deliver eDiscovery support for disputes, investigations, and transactional due diligence.
* Advise stakeholders on eDiscovery best practices, technology solutions, and defensible workflows to ensure efficient and compliant handling of electronically stored information.
* Support the selection, implementation, and ongoing management of eDiscovery platforms and tools, ensuring they meet the needs of both compliance and client-facing work.
* Coordinate data collection and preservation activities, working with IT, Information Security, and matter teams to ensure defensibility and chain of custody.
* Develop and maintain eDiscovery workflows, protocols, and quality control procedures to ensure consistency and accuracy across all projects.
* Provide training and support to fee earners, paralegals, and support staff on eDiscovery processes, tools, and technology-assisted review methodologies.
* Support the eDiscovery Manager, DPO and GCO team with data subject access requests (DSARs), file reviews, and other regulatory compliance matters as required.
* Liaise with external eDiscovery vendors and service providers, managing relationships and ensuring cost-effective delivery of services.
* Prepare and manage project budgets, timelines, and reporting, keeping stakeholders informed of progress and any issues.
* Stay current with developments in eDiscovery technology, legal requirements, and industry best practices, recommending improvements to the firm’s capabilities.
* Comply with all relevant legal and regulatory obligations including the Solicitors Regulation Authority (SRA) Standards and Regulations, and Principles.
**Skills and Experience**
Essential:
* Demonstrable experience in eDiscovery project management within a law firm, legal services provider, or corporate legal department.
* Strong working knowledge of eDiscovery platforms and tools (e.g. Relativity, Nuix, Concordance, or similar).
* Understanding of the litigation lifecycle, disclosure obligations under the Civil Procedure Rules, and data protection legislation including UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018.
* Experience managing data collection, processing, review, and production workflows.
* Strong project management skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and deliver to deadlines.
* Excellent communication skills with the ability to explain technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
Desirable:
* Relevant professional qualification or certification in eDiscovery, project management, or information governance (e.g. ACEDS, CIPP, PRINCE2, or equivalent).
* Experience with technology-assisted review (TAR), predictive coding, or AI-powered review tools.
* Experience handling data subject access requests (DSARs) and regulatory investigations.
* Knowledge of digital forensics principles and data preservation techniques.
* Experience working with external eDiscovery vendors and managing third-party service providers.
**Person Specification**
* Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to convey complex technical and legal concepts clearly to diverse audiences including fee earners, clients, and IT teams.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with a methodical approach to managing large volumes of data and identifying efficient solutions.
* Highly organised with meticulous attention to detail and the ability to maintain accuracy when working under pressure or to tight deadlines.
* Adaptable and resilient, able to respond effectively to changing priorities and manage competing demands across multiple projects.
* Collaborative team player who builds trusted working relationships and works effectively across departments and with external providers.
* Proactive and self-motivated, with the confidence to take ownership of projects and drive them through to completion.
* Commercial awareness with an understanding of how eDiscovery supports client service delivery and the firm’s business objectives.
* Commitment to continuous learning and staying current with developments in eDiscovery technology and best practices.

## **Why this role exists**
Every city, county, and school district buys things. Roads, software, cleaning services, IT infrastructure. The total is somewhere north of two trillion dollars a year. And almost all of it moves through procurement processes designed for a different era: slow; paper-heavy; opaque and exhausting for everyone involved.
Civic Marketplace was built to fix that. We're a modern, data-driven platform where government agencies discover, evaluate, and engage suppliers. Where businesses, especially smaller and growing ones, can actually find and win public sector work without needing a dedicated contracts team to navigate the maze.
We're past the point of proving this works. Agencies are live on the platform, real money moves through it, and we're now combining that marketplace infrastructure with AI in ways that could genuinely transform how procurement works. Not just incrementally but structurally.
None of it works without data that can be trusted. Procurement is a data problem before it is a software problem: who the suppliers actually are, what they can genuinely deliver, which contracts an agency is already entitled to buy from, what this thing cost the county next door. That information exists, scattered across thousands of agency portals, state registries and PDF attachments, in no agreed format, and nobody has assembled it properly. Whoever does gets to define how public money is spent for the next decade. That's this role.
## **The problem you'd own**
The hard part isn't moving data from one place to another. Any engineer here will tell you the pipelines are the easy half.
The hard part is that public procurement has no shared vocabulary. The same supplier turns up as four different legal entities across three registries, and two of the spellings are wrong. Commodity codes are applied inconsistently, or not at all. A cooperative contract one agency can buy from today is invisible to the agency next door because it was published as a PDF on a portal with no API. Every source you touch is incomplete, inconsistent, or both, and most of it is public record, so you can't quietly correct it. You have to model the mess honestly.
And the bar just moved. We recently launched an MCP integration that lets agencies request quotes through Claude, GPT and Copilot. When an agent answers a procurement question, a wrong answer doesn't read like a bug, it reads like advice, and in public spending, bad advice ends up in a council meeting. That puts weight on freshness, lineage and provenance that most product data layers never carry. As we build out our agentic procurement capabilities, the reliability of that data, and how we prepare it for retrieval, becomes our most critical engineering challenge.
So this is an entity resolution and data trust problem dressed as a pipeline problem, and it's yours to solve. You'd work out what is actually wrong with the data, which is rarely what everyone assumes, then build the fix so it holds for every source we add next. Not a script per source held together by whoever wrote it.
## **About the role**
You would be our first dedicated data engineering hire, reporting to Mikey Mo, our Head of Engineering. Data work today sits with the product engineering team and gets done alongside shipping features. It works, but it belongs to whoever last touched it, and that isn't a foundation for what comes next.
To give you a sense of the gap: awarded quotes that slip through the platform get manually caught by our commercial team and hand-entered into HubSpot instead. Supplier onboarding data follows the same pattern. So as and when the platform and HubSpot become out of sync, it makes it difficult to say with confidence which one is right.
This is a build-and-do role. You'd collaborate closely with our Head of Engineering to shape the architecture, and you'd also write the pipelines, carry the pager for them, and go and read the raw source when a number looks wrong. If you're looking for a role where you set direction in isolation and hand implementation to other people, this isn't it. If you want substantial responsibility and scope as a function lead alongside our Head of Engineering while still enjoying the craft yourself, it very much is.
You would not be starting from nothing. There's a live platform with real transactions running through it, a product engineering team who know where the bodies are buried, and access most people in this field would have to scrape for: Civic Marketplace is a member of the NIGP Business Council, with real partnerships across councils of governments. Most people doing this job spend their first year getting the data access. You'd start with the door already open.
## **What you'd own**
Five things, and the freedom to decide how.
1. **Trust in the data.** The north star. A golden, trusted dataset that powers Civic Marketplace's analytics, so when someone asks how many quotes were awarded last quarter, or how much GMV we've captured, there's one number, and it's right. You'd own the diagnosis and the fix.
2. **Ingestion.** Pipelines that pull supplier, agency, solicitation and contract data out of sources never designed to be read by anything but a person. Reliable, observable, and cheap enough to add the next source without a meeting about whether it's worth it.
3. **The canonical model.** One supplier, one record, across every spelling, trading name, subsidiary and registry identifier. One shared definition of a contract vehicle, a commodity, an agency, that product, sales and customer success all use and none of them argue with. This is the unglamorous part that makes everything downstream possible.
4. **The system underneath.** Testing, lineage and freshness, so when the platform tells an agency something we know where it came from and when. And self-serve data for product, customer success and analytics, so nobody queues behind an engineer for a number. Everything you build should work for the next source without you in the loop. This is where AI earns its place, turning what is currently hand-checked into something repeatable.
5. **Agentic data infrastructure.** As we scale our use of AI-native procurement, you will own the data layer that powers our agentic workflows. This goes beyond standard retrieval. You will design ingestion and storage strategies, including optimizing vector pipelines like Pinecone for RAG, to ensure our agents have the high-fidelity, context-aware data necessary to perform reliably in production.
You'd work closely with product engineering, customer success and our Growth Lead. Application feature work stays with the product engineering team, so you're not competing for that ground. You own the layer they build on top of.
## **How we use AI**
We use Claude daily, across content pipelines, community response and internal knowledge, and increasingly inside the product itself. That's real, not a line in a job ad.
For this role it cuts two ways. There's how you work: source profiling, schema mapping, test generation, the documentation that otherwise never gets written. Most of that is now automatable, and we expect you to automate it. And there's what you build: the data layer that decides whether agentic procurement is trustworthy or embarrassing. The second is the harder and more interesting problem.
What we care about is not whether you can use it. Everyone says they can. It's whether you reach for it to make something repeatable. The difference between someone who writes pipelines faster and someone who builds the tooling that means the next hundred sources don't each need hand-holding is the difference we're hiring for.
If you've built data quality tooling, evaluation harnesses, retrieval pipelines or automated documentation from scratch, tell us about them. If AI has changed how you think about the work and not just how fast you produce it, we especially want to hear that.

* Strong SQL and Python, and the judgement to know when the warehouse is the wrong place to solve a problem
* A data model you designed that other people had to live with, including the parts you would do differently now

Creandum's edge has always been people: the network, the judgment, the hustle. To sharpen our edge, we need to make everything those people learn compound: every meeting, every diligence process, every founder relationship feeding a shared foundation instead of evaporating into inboxes and individual heads.
You will build and own that foundation: the firm's data platform, the intelligence layer on top of it, and the governance that makes partners willing to trust it with their most sensitive work. This is a new function, and you are its first hire. You'll start hands-on-keyboard and stay that way for the time being; but you're building an estate the firm will run on, and the mandate grows with what you prove.
You report to the Operating Partner, but work directly and independently with every member of the firm.
We believe different viewpoints drive our growth, and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds.
What you'll own
The data platform. The firm's data architecture end to end: warehouse, ingestion from core systems (CRM, meeting transcripts, documents, email/calendar), entity resolution, and data quality. One person, one company, one deal – consistent across every source. This is foundational; everything else flows from it.
The intelligence layer. Retrieval, search & agent tooling that give everyone's AI real firm context, serving both individual workflows (bottom-up) and firm-wide platforms (top-down). Built for passive compounding: the system gets better as people work and as models improve, without depending on anyone's discipline.
Access, trust, and AI risk. The access model as structural enforcement, not instructions: who sees what, with identity, provenance, and audit. Sensitive fund and partner data protected to a standard the partnership will trust, plus the AI-specific risk judgment (injection containment, egress, tool guardrails) for everything the function ships, in collaboration with legal/regulatory counsel.
Technology strategy and the tool estate. Accountability for whether the firm's tools are the right ones: evaluation, integration, and replacement of the systems and data sources the firm runs on, in close partnership with the stakeholders who use them. Buy when buying is better; build when building is better. You have the mandate to choose, and then execute on your decision. Make sure security, compliance and budget are part of the equation.
What you'll deliver
First 6 months. A complete map of the firm's data and systems. The foundational data platform stood up. Two or three lightweight tools shipped that visibly improve how a team works. A clear, prioritized 12–18 month roadmap, authored by you and agreed with the partnership.
By 12 months. V1 of the firm's shared intelligence layer live and in daily use. The diligence process made genuinely multiplayer; firm knowledge and meeting history informing live deals instead of sitting unused. Measurable adoption, reported honestly, with failures killed as quickly as the wins are shipped.
Beyond. The roadmap is yours to define. Candidates for the frontier: productizing how the firm wins deals, network intelligence that answers "who do we know" in seconds, platform tools founders can self-serve, and operational automation across finance, events, and admin.
How you'll work
Builder first. You ship personally. This is not a role for someone who wants a team of ten doing the building.
Co-creation, not solo genius. Stakeholders across the firm (investment, platform, marketing, operations, etc.) steer, test, and tune what you build. Within a year, everyone at the firm should be able to point at something they had a hand in shaping.
Product discipline. Prototype, validate with real users, kill what doesn't get adopted. Usage is the metric; expect and budget for churn.
Scale deliberately. You start solo. As the foundation proves out, you'll orchestrate internal or external build resources and potentially grow the function. You are prepared to identify, leverage and lead exceptional talent to help achieve results.
Who you are
You've shipped a real data or AI product end to end (pipelines, retrieval, and the product surface) and people actually used it.
Deep, hands-on command of data architecture, warehousing, and governance. Fluent with embeddings, retrieval, and agents that act, not just answer.
You treat access control and provenance as product features, not compliance chores.
Low ego, high agency, energized by a blank page. Excited to tackle the unglamorous work (entity resolution, data hygiene, permissions) that everything depends on.
You can sit with an investor, an EA, and a founder in the same week and design for all of them. Venture experience isn't required, but you'll need to earn a front-line view of the work fast.
You can say "no" and "not yet" to smart, senior people and make them glad you did.
What this role is not
Not IT operations: endpoint, device & office infrastructure are handled by our managed IT partner.
Not reg compliance: policy & DORA workstreams are owned by legal, with your input on anything AI.
Not a reporting function: you build systems that answer questions, not dashboards on request.
Why this role
You'll have a blank page, real budget influence, direct partnership access, and a firm small enough that what you build touches everyone within weeks. The firms that figure this out will compound differently from the ones that don't. This is the seat where that happens.

## **Role overview:**
London Currys London Campus at Waterloo Permanent Full Time Grade 4
At Currys we're united by one passion: to help everyone enjoy amazing technology. As one of the best-known retailers of tech, we're proud of the service our customers receive and it's all down to our team of caring and committed colleagues. Join us and you'll work in a great team where you can be yourself and bring your personality. Working as one team, we learn and grow together, celebrating the big and small moments that make every day amazing. Currys is in the middle of one of the most ambitious AI and automation shifts in UK retail. We are rethinking how customers discover and buy technology, how stores operate, how supply chains move, and how colleagues do their best work. The AI & Monetisation function is where the boldest bets get placed. Supply chain is central to that shift. Every product we sell has to be in the right place, reach the customer as promised and, when it comes back, be returned to the supplier, refurbished or scrapped. Behind that sits a complex landscape of warehouse, order management and transport systems that is being modernised, and an experienced team that knows how it fits together. You'll lead our Supply Chain squad directly, owning the data and AI products across forward fulfilment and returns. This is a role for a builder. We're looking for someone who has seen what a modern, data-driven logistics operation looks like, can shape that into a vision that fits Currys, and can bring an experienced team and its stakeholders with them as they move to a product way of working. You'll partner with your squad's engineers, our Platform Engineering team and colleagues with deep supply chain knowledge, alongside senior leaders across Logistics and Home Delivery, to identify opportunities, rapidly prototype and then take solutions into production. You'll work with source system owners and the teams leading our supply chain transformation programmes, and engage with IT Operations, InfoSec and Enablement on shared infrastructure, AI capabilities and governance. You'll also coach and develop the Technical Product Manager you manage, and influence stakeholders at every level, from warehouse and delivery teams to senior leadership.
## **Key responsibilities:**
**You’ll build products with a modern data and AI stack: Claude Code, Databricks, dbt, and Omni. Additionally, you’ll need to:**
* Shape the data and AI product vision for Currys' logistics operation, bringing an outside-in view of what good looks like and turning it into a roadmap that operational leaders support
* Own the Supply Chain roadmap, covering forward fulfilment (stock, warehousing, transport and last mile) and returns (collection, receipt and onward routing)
* Manage and coach a Technical Product Manager, setting expectations, reviewing their work, and staying accountable for the roadmap they run day to day
* Lead discovery on the harder, more ambiguous problems: the ones that cut across the operation, have no obvious single owner, or need alignment from multiple senior stakeholders before they can start
* Establish product ways of working with a team and stakeholder group used to working from requests: a single route for new demand, discovery before build, and a prioritised roadmap with clear expectations of what will be delivered and when
* Agree data contracts with source system owners, so that data quality and integration issues are resolved at source rather than worked around downstream
* Determine the future of the existing reports and applications: which are replaced by new data products and which are retired, rather than rebuilt like for like on the new platform
* Run agile ceremonies, quarterly OKR setting and roadmap readouts across your squads, giving stakeholders one coherent view aligned to the wider AI & Monetisation roadmap
**Required Skills & Experience:**
* 6 years of experience in technical product management, working with data and analytics products, and LLM / ML solutions, including some experience leading or mentoring other Product Managers or Analysts
* Significant experience in supply chain, logistics or fulfilment, ideally in e-commerce, third-party logistics or a retailer with mature data and AI capability, and a clear point of view on what a modern, data-driven logistics operation looks like
* Working knowledge of supply chain systems (warehouse, order and transport management, and planning) and the data they produce, including the challenges of integrating them
* Demonstrated comfort working directly with engineers: you do not need to write production code, but you need to hold your own in technical conversations
* Extensive experience using AI tools to automate and improve your own workflows and your team's, with a clear point of view on how AI can improve the products you build
* Experience with agile delivery in cross-functional squads, including backlog management, sprint ceremonies, and OKR frameworks, ideally including introducing product ways of working to a team or stakeholder group new to them
* Strong stakeholder management skills with operational leaders, including the ability to manage competing priorities, push back constructively, and reset expectations where needed
* Familiarity with modern data stack concepts: medallion architecture, dimensional modelling, data lakes, semantic layers, or equivalent. Experience replacing legacy reports and systems during a platform migration would be an advantage
* Degree in a technical or business field, or equivalent experience
* You're a product builder: building POCs and prototypes rather than relying on others
* Cultivate meaningful relationships with your stakeholders, lead with empathy and foster a culture of collaboration with your peers
* Take real satisfaction in helping other Product Managers get better at the job, not just doing it well yourself
* Build your understanding of an operation first-hand, and are credible with warehouse teams and senior leaders alike
## **Why join us:**
**We know our people are the secret to our success. That's why we're always looking for ways to reward great work. You'll find a host of benefits designed to work for you, including:**
* 25 days of annual leave (plus bank holiday entitlement) and a competitive pension scheme
* Private Medical Insurance
* Life Assurance
* Fantastic colleague discounts on Tech with Currys and iD Mobile
* Hybrid working (with an expectation to meet in person 2-4 times per month)
Join our team and we’ll be with you every step of the way, helping you develop the career you want with new opportunities, on-going training and skills for life.
Not only can you shape your own future, but you can help take charge of ours too. As the biggest recycler and repairer of tech in the UK, we’re in a position to make a real impact on people and the planet.
Every voice has a space at our table and we’re committed to making inclusion and diversity part of everything we do, including how we strengthen our workforce. **The role**
As the Viewer Advocacy Operations Manager, you will serve as the operational bridge between our internal business and our outsourced business process outsourcing (BPO) partners. Your core mandate is to ensure the vendor consistently meets or exceeds Service Level Agreements (SLAs), quality standards, and customer experience goals.
You will not directly manage frontline agents; instead, you will hold the vendor’s Site Operations Managers accountable, diving deep into weekly metrics, managing real-time deviations, and driving rapid, tactical improvements on the floor.
**Main responsibilities**
**Daily & Weekly Performance Management**
* Intraday & Daily Monitoring: Monitor real-time queues, Service Levels, and key metrics (AHT, FCR, Abandonment Rate) across vendor sites to ensure intra-day staffing and performance align with forecasts.
* Weekly Business Reviews (WBRs): Lead weekly performance calls with vendor management and internal teams. Analyse the previous week’s performance, identify root causes for target misses, and agree on immediate corrective action plans.
* WFM & Staffing Alignment: Collaborate with Senior Viewer Advocacy Manager and the vendor’s WFM teams to validate short-term volume forecasts, lock in weekly schedules, and manage shrinkage, absenteeism, and attrition risks.

**Quality, Process & Escalations**
* Quality Calibration: Partner with internal and vendor Quality Assurance (QA) teams to conduct weekly calibration sessions. Ensure the vendor is grading contacts accurately and delivering effective coaching to their agents.
* Escalation Management: Serve as the primary point of escalation for critical customer incidents, system outages, or critical agent errors generated at the vendor site.
* Tactical Process Improvement: Identify friction points in the agent experience (e.g., clunky tools, outdated knowledge base articles) based on weekly trend analysis and deploy rapid fixes to improve handle times and first-contact resolution.
* **Day to Day Operational questions: Fielding day to day operational questions and providing direction to the operation on handling outlier queries.**
* Communications & Briefings: Ensure product updates, policy changes, and marketing promotions are effectively communicated to and understood by the vendor’s frontline staff.
**Vendor Relationship Management**
* Partnership Dynamics: Build a strong, collaborative, yet accountable relationship with vendor operational leadership. Balance the need for strict SLA enforcement with a supportive partnership approach.

* Solid operational experience in a multi-channel contact centre environment, with experience of directly managing BPO/outsourced vendors (either from the client side or as a BPO Operations Manager).
* Strong ability to manipulate and interpret contact centre data using Excel/Google Sheets. Must be able to read an interval report and immediately spot anomalies.
* Proven ability to have difficult performance conversations with external partners and drive them toward immediate action without having direct HR authority over their staff.
**Other things we’re looking for** (key criteria)
* Urgency & Bias for Action: Thrives in a fast-paced environment where daily performance dictates success.
* Root-Cause Thinker: Doesn’t just accept “volume was high” as an excuse; digs into why volume was high and how the vendor responded.
* Resilience: Capable of maintaining focus and keeping calm during unexpected system outages or sudden volume spikes.

# Research Staff, Voice AI Foundations [UK - Remote]
## Location
London, UK

OverviewApplication
# **Company Overview**
Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.
# **Company Operating Rhythm**
At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.
Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.
Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.
## The Opportunity
Voice is the most natural modality for human interaction with machines. However, current sequence modeling paradigms based on jointly scaling model and data cannot deliver voice AI capable of universal human interaction. The challenges are rooted in fundamental data problems posed by audio: real-world audio data is scarce and enormously diverse, spanning a vast space of voices, speaking styles, and acoustic conditions. Even if billions of hours of audio were accessible, its inherent high dimensionality creates computational and storage costs that make training and deployment prohibitively expensive at world scale. We believe that entirely new paradigms for audio AI are needed to overcome these challenges and make voice interaction accessible to everyone.
## The Role
As a Member of the Research Staff, you will pioneer the development of Latent Space Models (LSMs), a new approach that aims to solve the fundamental data, scale, and cost challenges associated with building robust, contextualized voice AI. Your research will focus on solving one or more of the following problems:
* Build next-generation neural audio codecs that achieve extreme, low bit-rate compression and high fidelity reconstruction across a world-scale corpus of general audio.
* Pioneer steerable generative models that can synthesize the full diversity of human speech from the codec latent representation, from casual conversation to highly emotional expression to complex multi-speaker scenarios with environmental noise and overlapping speech.
* Develop embedding systems that cleanly factorize the codec latent space into interpretable dimensions of speaker, content, style, environment, and channel effects -- enabling precise control over each aspect and the ability to massively amplify an existing seed dataset through “latent recombination”.
* Leverage latent recombination to generate synthetic audio data at previously impossible scales, unlocking joint model and data scaling paradigms for audio. Endeavor to train multimodal speech-to-speech systems that can 1) understand any human irrespective of their demographics, state, or environment and 2) produce empathic, human-like responses that achieve conversational or task-oriented objectives.
* Design model architectures, training schemes, and inference algorithms that are adapted for hardware at the bare metal enabling cost efficient training on billion-hour datasets and powering real-time inference for hundreds of millions of concurrent conversations.
## The Challenge
We are seeking researchers who:
* See "unsolved" problems as opportunities to pioneer entirely new approaches
* Can identify the one critical experiment that will validate or kill an idea in days, not months
* Have the vision to scale successful proofs-of-concept 100x
* Are obsessed with using AI to automate and amplify your own impact
If you find yourself energized rather than daunted by these expectations—if you're already thinking about five ideas to try while reading this—you might be the researcher we need. This role demands obsession with the problems, creativity in approach, and relentless drive toward elegant, scalable solutions. The technical challenges are immense, but the potential impact is transformative.
## It's Important to Us That You Have
* Strong mathematical foundation in statistical learning theory, particularly in areas relevant to self-supervised and multimodal learning
* Deep expertise in foundation model architectures, with an understanding of how to scale training across multiple modalities
* Proven ability to bridge theory and practice—someone who can both derive novel mathematical formulations and implement them efficiently
* Demonstrated ability to build data pipelines that can process and curate massive datasets while maintaining quality and diversity
* Track record of designing controlled experiments that isolate the impact of architectural innovations and validate theoretical insights
* Experience optimizing models for real-world deployment, including knowledge of hardware constraints and efficiency techniques
* History of open-source contributions or research publications that have advanced the state of the art in speech/language AI
# Ideal Researcher Profile
An ideal researcher, as evidenced by the recurring themes across these foundational papers, excels in five key areas: (1) Statistical & Mathematical Foundations, (2) Algorithmic Innovation & Implementation, (3) Data-Driven & Scalable Systems, (4) Hardware & Systems Understanding, and (5) Rigorous Experimental Design. Below is a synthesis of how each paper highlights these qualities, with references illustrating why they matter for building robust, impactful deep learning models.
## **1. Statistical & Mathematical Foundations**
**Mastery of Core Concepts**
Many papers, like Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models and Neural Discrete Representation Learning (VQ-VAE), reflect the importance of power-law analyses, derivation of novel losses, or adaptation of fundamental equations (e.g., in VQ-VAE's commitment loss or rectified flows in Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers). Such mathematical grounding clarifies why models converge or suffer collapse.
**Combining Existing Theories in Novel Ways**
Papers such as Moshi (combining text modeling, audio codecs, and hierarchical generative modeling) and Finite Scalar Quantization (FSQ's adaptation of classic scalar quantization to replace vector-quantized representations) show how reusing but reimagining known techniques can yield breakthroughs. Many references (e.g., the structured state-space duality in Transformers are SSMs) underscore how unifying previously separate research lines can reveal powerful algorithmic or theoretical insights.
**Logical Reasoning and Assumption Testing**
Across all papers—particularly in the problem statements of Whisper or Rectified Flow Transformers—the authors present assumptions (e.g., "scaling data leads to zero-shot robustness" or "straight-line noise injection improves sample efficiency") and systematically verify them with thorough empirical results. An ideal researcher similarly grounds new ideas in well-formed, testable hypotheses.
## **2. Algorithmic Innovation & Implementation**
**Creative Solutions to Known Bottlenecks**
Each paper puts forth a unique algorithmic contribution—Rectified Flow Transformers redefines standard diffusion paths, FSQ proposes simpler scalar quantizations contrasted with VQ, phi-3 mini relies on curated data and blocksparse attention, and Mamba-2 merges SSM speed with attention concepts.
**Turning Theory into Practice**
Whether it's the direct preference optimization (DPO) for alignment in phi-3 or the residual vector quantization in SoundStream, these works show that bridging design insights with implementable prototypes is essential.
**Clear Impact Through Prototypes & Open-Source**
Many references (Whisper, neural discrete representation learning, Mamba-2) highlight releasing code or pretrained models, enabling the broader community to replicate and build upon new methods. This premise of collaboration fosters faster progress.
## **3. Data-Driven & Scalable Systems**
**Emphasis on Large-Scale Data and Efficient Pipelines**
Papers such as Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision (Whisper) and BASE TTS demonstrate that collecting and processing hundreds of thousands of hours of real-world audio can unlock new capabilities in zero-shot or low-resource domains. Meanwhile, phi-3 Technical Report shows that filtering and curating data at scale (e.g., "data optimal regime") can yield high performance even in smaller models.
**Strategic Use of Data for Staged Training**
A recurring strategy is to vary sources of data or the order of tasks. Whisper trains on multilingual tasks, BASE TTS uses subsets/stages for pretraining on speech tokens, and phi-3 deploys multiple training phases (web data, then synthetic data). This systematic approach to data underscores how an ideal researcher designs training curricula and data filtering protocols for maximum performance.
## **4. Hardware & Systems Understanding**
**Efficient Implementations at Scale**
Many works illustrate how researchers tune architectures for modern accelerators: the In-Datacenter TPU paper exemplifies domain-specific hardware design for dense matrix multiplications, while phi-3 leverages blocksparse attention and custom Triton kernels to run advanced LLMs on resource-limited devices.
**Real-Time & On-Device Constraints**
SoundStream shows how to compress audio in real time on a smartphone CPU, demonstrating that knowledge of hardware constraints (latency, limited memory) drives design choices. Similarly, Moshi's low-latency streaming TTS and phi-3-mini's phone-based inference highlight that an ideal researcher must adapt algorithms to resource limits while maintaining robustness.
**Architectural & Optimization Details**
Papers like Mamba-2 in Transformers are SSMs and the In-Datacenter TPU work show how exploiting specialized matrix decomposition, custom memory hierarchies, or quantization approaches can lead to breakthroughs in speed or energy efficiency.
## **5. Rigorous Experimental Design**
**Controlled Comparisons & Ablations**
Nearly all papers—Whisper, FSQ, Mamba-2, BASE TTS—use systematic ablations to isolate the impact of individual components (e.g., ablation on vector-quantization vs. scalar quantization in FSQ, or size of codebooks in VQ-VAEs). This approach reveals which design decisions truly matter.
**Multifold Evaluation Metrics**
From MUSHRA listening tests (SoundStream, BASE TTS) to FID in image synthesis (Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers, FSQ) to perplexity or zero-shot generalization in language (phi-3, Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models), the works demonstrate the value of comprehensive, carefully chosen metrics.
**Stress Tests & Edge Cases**
Whisper's out-of-distribution speech benchmarks, SoundStream's evaluation on speech + music, or Mamba-2's performance on multi-query associative recall demonstrate the importance of specialized challenge sets. Researchers who craft or adopt rigorous benchmarks and "red-team" their models (as in phi-3 safety alignment) are better prepared to address real-world complexities.
## Summary
Overall, an ideal researcher in deep learning consistently demonstrates:
* A solid grounding in theoretical and statistical principles
* A talent for proposing and validating new algorithmic solutions
* The capacity to orchestrate data pipelines that scale and reflect real-world diversity
* Awareness of hardware constraints and system-level trade-offs for efficiency
* Thorough and transparent experimental practices
These qualities surface across research on speech (Whisper, BASE TTS), language modeling (Scaling Laws, phi-3), specialized hardware (TPU, Transformers are SSMs), and new representation methods (VQ-VAE, FSQ, SoundStream). By balancing these attributes—rigorous math, innovative algorithms, large-scale data engineering, hardware-savvy optimizations, and reproducible experimentation—researchers can produce impactful, trustworthy advancements in foundational deep learning.
## Foundational Papers
This job description was generated through analysis of the following papers:
* Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision (arXiv:2212.04356)
* Moshi: a speech-text foundation model for real-time dialogue (arXiv:2410.00037)
* Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers for High-Resolution Image Synthesis (arXiv:2403.03206)
* Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models (arXiv:2001.08361)
* BASE TTS: Lessons from building a billion-parameter Text-to-Speech model on 100K hours of data (arXiv:2402.08093)
* In-Datacenter Performance Analysis of a Tensor Processing Unit (arXiv:1704.04760)
* Neural Discrete Representation Learning (arXiv:1711.00937)
* SoundStream: An End-to-End Neural Audio Codec (arXiv:2107.03312)
* Finite Scalar Quantization: VQ-VAE Made Simple (arXiv:2309.15505)
* Phi-3 Technical Report: A Highly Capable Language Model Locally on Your Phone (arXiv:2404.14219)
* Transformers are SSMs: Generalized Models and Efficient Algorithms Through Structured State Space Duality (arXiv:2405.21060)
