# Product Management Senior Expert
* Full-time
## Company Description
*Work smart, have fun and make an impact!* **EcoVadis is the leading provider of business sustainability ratings**. Our solutions are backed by an international team of experts and powerful technology. We analyze data and build sustainability scorecards that give companies actionable insights into their environmental, social and ethical risks. **Why apply to EcoVadis?** Be a part of the global sustainability change in business. Grow your career. Work with extraordinary people. Feel valued for your contribution. Learn more about our team and culture on EcoVadis careers page.
## Job Description
As a Senior Product Manager for one of our Strategic Use Cases, you will own that use case end-to-end — from the customer problem and the data it depends on, through prototype, roadmap and launch, to the outcome in the market. You will work alongside senior engineers and product experts to define the ambition, understand requirements and launch innovative new products.
This is a builder role, not a coordination role. We're looking for a high-agency generalist who prototypes before they debate, uses AI to move at a different speed, engages customers directly, and takes full ownership of outcomes — not output.
**What you'll be doing**
* Own the vision: Set and drive the aligned, end-to-end vision for your use case (regulatory due diligence, human rights due diligence, decarbonization or resilience)— what the customer experience should be, where the gaps are, and the sequence from parity to leadership.
* Understand the market: Understand the technical requirements of your use case, and how other competitors and customers are currently solving it. Take inspiration from everywhere, including partner discussions, conferences, webinars and other resources.
* Engage customers directly: Spend real time with buyers, program owners and co-development accounts. Validate problems and solutions first-hand; and build interest from customers and prospects.
* Prototype with AI: Use AI prototyping tools to build working demos, spin up lightweight services and test your own assumptions before committing engineering. Show the team what's possible by doing it, not describing it.
* Drive the build forward: Work alongside engineering to unblock and drive the build forward, working across multiple areas of the product and platform, collaborating with other tribes and squads whilst executing independently or in partnership.
* Partner on go-to-market: Work hand-in-hand with the Strategic Use Case Leads and commercial teams to land what you build.
* Own the outcome: Define the measures of success, hold yourself and the circle to them, and lead clean persist / pivot / stop decisions.
**Who you are**
* A generalist builder at heart — you move fluidly between strategy, data, prototype and GTM, and you'd rather build a rough thing that teaches you something than debate a perfect thing that doesn't.
* An AI-native operator — AI is woven through how you work: discovery, analysis, prototyping, instrumentation and communication.
* Customer-obsessed — you get your conviction from talking to real customers, not from the building.
* Biased to speed — you move decisively with incomplete information, tell reversible decisions from irreversible ones, and update fast when you're wrong. Strong opinions, loosely held.
* Comfortable without full control — part of your use case's scope and experience will always be owned by other squads. You see managing that, as the craft.
* Mission-driven — you want your work to help guide all companies toward a sustainable world, and to help EcoVadis lead the market in getting there.
**AI fluency we hire for**
We expect you to operate at the AI-Fluent to AI-Native end of the spectrum: you don't just use AI for one-off tasks, you reconstruct core PM workflows around it — agents configured with your product context, personas and prior research; machine-testable acceptance criteria; reusable workflows you share with the squad. At the top of this ladder, the PM shifts from feature author to outcome orchestrator — concentrating on strategic trade-offs and novel bets while agents carry more of the discovery and synthesis.
## Qualifications
* Typically 10+ years experience, including a track record owning a meaningful product area end-to-end in B2B enterprise SaaS, with real business and customer outcomes to point to.
* Enough technical fluency to build — you can prototype with AI tooling, LLM APIs and a scripting language (Python / JavaScript or equivalent) without waiting for engineering to validate every idea.
* An AI-native way of working that's already part of how you operate, not an aspiration.
* Comfort operating in a regulated, data-rich, sustainability or risk domain — or the curiosity and speed to get there fast.
* Sharp problem framing and communication — you walk into the room with a recommendation, not an open question, and you make engineering and design faster by reducing ambiguity.
* Be fluent in English (as our primary working language).
## Additional Information
In return for your expertise, we offer:
* Support with all the necessary office and IT equipment
* Flexible working hours
* Wellness allowance for mental and physical wellbeing
* Access to professional mental health support
* Referral bonus policy
* Learning and development
* Sustainability events and community involvement
* Peer recognition program
* Employee-led resource groups
* Cycle to work scheme
* Remote work from abroad policy
* Hybrid work organization (2 office days per week)
* Pension contributions and optional private health coverage
* Internet and electricity bill allowance
* Life Insurance
* Subsidised travel in London
* Community service day when volunteering
**Our hiring team looks forward to reviewing your resume, in English, with a guaranteed response to every application. A new job with purpose awaits you!**
**Don’t meet all criteria?** Please apply anyway. We welcome diverse candidates and want to assess your skills and potential contribution to EcoVadis, regardless of your background.

We want all candidates, including people with disabilities, people with long-term health conditions, and neurodiverse applicants, to feel confident demonstrating their potential. If you require adjustments, such as interview questions in advance, please inform the hiring team.

# Senior Analyst
At Edge Health, we believe that data and analytics have the potential to transform decision making, policy, quality and efficiency within the NHS. We are an analytics firm based in London, delivering consultancy services and developing data products to help unlock this potential for our clients. We are looking for a Senior Analyst to join our team full-time in London. Our consulting business focusses on both the delivery of projects to meet clients’ needs, and the development of repeatable propositions to take to market. We are growing quickly as a business and are looking for an individual with 2-4 years of professional experience, ideally in a consulting or healthcare analytics background who can integrate quickly into our team and support the growth of our consulting business. The organisations we work with have a wide range of needs, and differing levels of technical sophistication. We are committed to delivering work which brings the maximum benefit to our clients, patients, and the NHS, and doing this requires flexibility in the analytical approach we bring to each problem and an innovative mindset to use the best tools to get there. Key skills and competencies we are looking for include:
* Passion for working in healthcare, and experience of having done so;
* Technical skills and experience, such as data economics, statistics, coding, data science or modelling;
* Passion for working with people, experience in managing clients and analysts;
* Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, across a diverse range of areas;
* Enthusiasm for working closely with our clients and partner organisations as well as with other members of the Edge team.
**What's it like to work at Edge?**
The role is a mix of hands-on analysis and project delivery. As a Senior Analyst you run projects day to day and help oversee analysts and engineers, supported by a project manager and led by a Director. You'll still spend much of your time in the detail: coding in SQL, R or Python, building models, and working out what the results mean for the client.
The work is varied and often starts with a question rather than a prescribed method. We might be helping an NHS team understand pressures on a service, evaluating the economics of a new intervention, or building a tool that lets a client answer the question themselves. Because consulting, economics, data science and engineering sit closely together, people can move between these kinds of problems.
We are also small enough for people to shape what Edge does. Senior Analysts contribute to bids and scoping, help develop new propositions, and support the development of the wider team. We set aside two training days each quarter, and recent internal development time has produced new public tools as well as client propositions.
Edge is rated 4.9/5 on Glassdoor with 100% saying they would recommend the company. Recent reviews mention a supportive culture, interesting projects, personal development and lots of room to explore interests.
## Key Responsibilities
Key responsibilities within this role include:
* Project delivery: Taking responsibility for the day-to-day delivery of projects, overseeing analysts/engineers and overseen by Consultant or Senior Consultant and led by a Director;
* Applying technical & industry expertise: Bringing economics, modelling and/or healthcare experience to deliver high-quality outputs for our clients;
* Planning/project management: Converting client asks into actionable and realistic project plans, including technical details of required solution. Executing said plan with regular client and stakeholder engagement;
* Innovation: Proactively learning from past projects and experiences to build and develop new propositions for use within the health sector and improving the way we use data;
* Business development: Supporting the wider growth of Edge, through development of marketing material and team training and development;
* Leadership: Leading small teams/individuals and supporting in the technical/personal development of individuals;
* Contributing to our siles pipeline: Contributing to writing scope documents, bidding material and responses to tender requests.
## Desired Skills & Experience
We greatly value diversity and would welcome applicants from a range of academic and professional backgrounds. While meeting all the stated job requirements can be beneficial, at Edge, we understand that diverse experiences and perspectives can bring great value to our work. So, if you're passionate about the work we do and share our values, we encourage you to apply, even if you don't meet every single criterion.
* Be highly motivated, self-driven and versatile, and excited to work within a small and growing team;
* Technical skills in the fields of data science, economics, engineering or statistics developed either through academia or professional experience;
* Have the ability to engage effectively and enjoyably with a range of people, and to communicate impactfully the findings and implications of their work;
* Have knowledge and experience working with data, with strong skills in languages such as SQL, R and Python;
* 2-4 years of professional experience, working in a healthcare, consulting, research, modelling, product or related setting;
* Have experience of delivering projects and outputs to tight timescales and to a high quality; including delegating work to more junior team members, planning and scoping;
* Take proactive responsibility for personal development, and the development of individuals and teams around them.

Edge Health is a boutique analytics firm of around 40 economists, data scientists and data engineers with backgrounds in economics, statistics, epidemiology, policy, management consulting and healthcare. We have worked for many years with NHS hospitals and policymakers, and are familiar with their challenges. We use new and diverse technologies centred around use of data to solve these issues at scale.
Since our formation in April 2017, we have grown rapidly and worked with more than 50 NHS organisations, including trusts, commissioners and regulators.
We are a client-facing organisation that sees the value in being close to the challenges we are helping to solve. We spend time working alongside our clients and enjoy seeing the direct impact of our work on patients and people who work in the NHS. Read more about the solutions we provide here.

## About The Role
Job title: Head of Education and Player Care. Responsible to: Academy Manager.
Bradford City AFC Academy is recruiting a Head of Education and Player Care. While the role is designed as a full-time position covering both specialisms, we value expertise and welcome applications tailored to either or both areas, as detailed below: • Option A: Full-Time Role – Head of Education & Player Care (40 hours per week) • Option B: Part-Time Specialist – Head of Education (20 hours per week) • Option C: Part-Time Specialist – Player Care Lead (20 hours per week)
Working within our Category 3 Academy, you will build a positive, supportive environment where young players can thrive in their schoolwork, personal lives, and overall well-being alongside their football development across all age groups.
A candidate taking on the combined full-time role will oversee both areas below, while part-time specialists will focus on their chosen 20-hour role.
**Education (20 Hours per Week)** • Plan, deliver, and track the Academy Education Programme in line with EFL and League Football Education (LFE) guidelines. • Oversee the delivery of the BTEC Sport qualification and apprenticeship framework for U18 scholars. • Maintain regular contact with local schools for younger players, monitoring attendance, academic progress, and day-release schedules. • Accurately maintain all educational records on required academy tracking systems. • Prepare players for life after football by facilitating career guidance and vocational training options.
**Player Care (20 Hours per Week)** • Act as the primary point of contact for player care across all age groups, promoting emotional well-being, mental health awareness, and personal growth. • Design and deliver engaging, age-appropriate Life Skills workshops covering topics such as online safety, financial literacy, health, and mental well-being. • Guide young players and their families through critical Academy transitions, including induction, scholarship signing, and exit/release strategies. • Work closely with the Academy Safeguarding Lead to maintain a safe, inclusive, and supportive environment. • Support players and families with transport and general welfare logistics as needed.
**Other requirements:** • Positively represent the culture and values of the Academy in every interaction. • Maintain professional boundaries at all times, adhere strictly to operational policies • Undertake any other reasonable duties, as requested by your Line Manager. • Work within and adhere to all Academy policies and procedures, maintaining a strong understanding of Bradford City AFC's culture and values.
**Selection process** Recruitment for this post will be conducted in two stages: • Stage One: Shortlisted candidates will attend an interview at Valley Parade. • Stage Two: Candidates moving to Stage Two will be invited to the Academy to give a short presentation on their chosen area (Education, Player Care, or both) and complete a practical task.
## About The Candidate
**About you**
• You are a friendly, well-organised, and caring professional with experience in teaching, pastoral care, or youth work. • You understand the pressures young athletes face as they look to balance and maintain schoolwork with their football. • You have strong administrative skills and are confident using software. • You enjoy working alongside coaches, medical staff, sports scientists, and parents. • You communicate clearly and build good relationships with schools and football governing bodies like the LFE.
**Qualifications and requirement's**
Essential (Options A, B and C) • Valid FA Safeguarding Children Certificate. • Emergency First Aid in Football (EFAiF) or equivalent valid first aid qualification. • Satisfactory Disclosure from an Enhanced DBS Check with Children’s Barred List clearance (This will need to be completed prior to appointment). Essential (Options A and B Only) • Qualified Teacher Status (QTS), PGCE, or Level 5+ teaching qualification.
Desirable (Options A, B and C) • Mental Health First Aid qualification (Youth or Adult). • Safeguarding training. • Proven experience working within an EFL/LFE framework or Premier League/EFL Academy environment. • Experience in using academy management software (e.g., PMA, Kitman Labs, or similar player-tracking platforms. • Full UK Driving Licence
## About The Club
**General terms** Working arrangement: Based at the Club’s Academy in Bradford, West Yorkshire (BD10 0NR).
Work environment: Indoor v Outdoor: Office, classroom and meeting spaces, with regular time spent pitch side and around academy training areas during sessions.
Physical Demands: Mostly office and classroom-based. Requirement to be able to access and move freely around the academy grounds. #
Volume and Pace: Busy, supportive youth sport environment operating under football academy regulations.
Liaison and Collaboration: Positive daily interaction within a Multi-Disciplinary Team (MDT) as well as maintaining clear, professional communication with players, parents and guardians. Safeguarding and Culture: Regulated environment requiring adherence to Club Safeguarding policies, professional boundaries, and Equality, Diversity & Inclusion (EDI) standards. Working days and times: Standard office hours with the flexibility to work evenings and weekends as needed.
Contract: Full-time/Part-time, Permanent.
Uniform: Bradford City AFC branded staff kit.

We are committed to being an inclusive employer. If you require any reasonable adjustments or accommodations due to a disability, neurodivergence, or health condition, please let us know how we can best support you during the application or interview stage.

We are fully committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people, and adults at risk, and we expect all staff, coaches, volunteers, and contractors to share this commitment and actively promote their welfare at all times.As part of our safer recruitment processes, this role involves working directly with children within an elite football environment. Applicants are required to disclose all convictions, cautions, reprimands, and final warnings, including those considered ‘spent’ under the provisions of the Act. • Any offer of employment is conditional upon receiving at least two satisfactory professional references (one of which must be your current or most recent employer) and proof of right to work in the UK. Having a criminal record will not automatically bar an applicant from working with us; every case is assessed individually based on the nature of the role and the background details disclosed.

## Description
**About Euromonitor**
Euromonitor International leads the world in data analytics and research into markets, industries, economies and consumers. We provide truly global insight and data on thousands of products and services; we are the first destination for organisations seeking growth. With our guidance, our clients can make bold, strategic decisions with confidence.
**Building the marketing department for the future**
Marketing at Euromonitor is being reimagined. We're building an AI-powered growth engine: agentic, automated, and data and tech led. A B2B marketing system designed for 2030, not 2015.
Behind it sits an advantage most companies would envy: original research from analysts across 210 markets, and decades of proprietary data built over more than 50 years. Our job is to turn that into growth.
And not incremental growth. We're not here for 10% better. We're building for 10x, and then 100x. That ambition sets the standard for everything we do, and everyone we hire.
So this is for people who want to drive transformation, not wait for it. Restless. Ambitious. More interested in building the engine than operating one someone else designed. If that sounds like you, this is a rare moment to join Euromonitor, and something special to be part of
**Purpose of the role**
This role owns the propositions, messaging and positioning for Euromonitor's syndicated portfolio: the research, the data, the platform and the technology behind it. You are the source of truth for what we sell, who it is for, why it wins, and how it is talked about in every market we operate in.
It sits at the intersection of product and technology on one side and commercial on the other, and it works in both directions: translating product and technology strategy into propositions clients understand and buy, and carrying client and market insight back so it shapes roadmap and prioritisation. Strategic in scope, hands-on in delivery. You set the direction, then write the words that carry it.
**Key accountabilities**
* Own the propositions, messaging and positioning for the syndicated portfolio, from the top-level narrative to product-level value propositions, and keep them the agreed source of truth everyone sells from.
* Translate product and technology strategy into client-ready propositions: the audiences, the problems we solve, the proof points and the competitive claims, written as a narrative colleagues can build from.
* Carry client, market and competitive insight back to product and technology leadership so that it shapes roadmap, packaging and prioritisation decisions.
* Equip commercial and client-facing teams with the messaging, tools and training needed to improve adoption, conversion and retention.
* Define and maintain target audience and use-case frameworks to ensure propositions resonate across industries, functions and product ICPs
* Mine usage, adoption, pipeline, renewal and competitive data for opportunities and risks across the portfolio, and turn what you find into positioning and commercial recommendations.
* Own go-to-market for launches and releases: the story, the assets and the enablement that make commercial teams fluent from day one, working alongside colleagues in the UK, US and other regions.
* Establish a continuous customer insight programme, bringing client, market and competitive feedback into proposition, roadmap and go-to-market decisions
* Build the competitive view for the portfolio: who we win against, where we lose, and the proposition, pricing and packaging responses that change the outcome.
**What success looks like;**
* One current proposition and messaging set for the portfolio, used consistently by marketing, sales and client-facing colleagues in their own conversations.
* Positioning that shows up commercially: strong win rates against named competitors, and deal quality that reflects the full value of the portfolio.
* Roadmap, packaging and prioritisation decisions that visibly reflect the client and market insight you bring.
* Launches that land with a clear story, measurable pipeline contribution and adoption that holds well beyond the launch window.
**What we're looking for**
* 6+ years in product marketing, including ownership of the positioning and messaging for a portfolio or product line rather than execution of someone else's.
* All experience must be in B2B marketing: a B2C-only background won't fit this role.

# Founding Account Executive / GTM Lead - AI SaaS
We are searching for an ambitious and commercially astute **Founding Account Executive/GTM Sales Lead** to join a fast-growing, early-stage AI SaaS business. You will combine hands-on new business development with strategic input, creating your own pipeline, leading complex sales conversations and closing new business. With significant influence over the company's go-to-market (GTM) strategy, sales processes and future growth, this role offers a genuine opportunity to build something rather than simply inherit an established playbook.

* **Uncapped commission**
* **Equity** in a fast-growing technology business
* **Based in Leeds -** Hybrid working (3-4 office days per week)
* **25 Days Holiday** + Bank Holidays
* **Access to best-in-class software and tools** to help you perform at your best

**The Role**
Working closely with the Founder, you will play a key role in executing and refining the company's go-to-market (GTM) strategy, combining hands-on new business development with strategic input to create pipeline, lead complex sales conversations and close new business.
This is not a position where you will simply manage inbound opportunities. You will be expected to pick up the phone, identify new markets and accounts, test different outbound approaches and maintain momentum throughout the sales process.
Alongside your individual sales responsibilities, you will help establish the processes, structure and messaging required to support a scalable sales function. You will also provide day-to-day direction to a Sales Development Representative and play an active role in the future development of the commercial team.
**Key Responsibilities:**
* Own the complete sales cycle, from initial prospecting and discovery through to negotiation and close.
* Build and maintain a high-quality pipeline through outbound activity, account research and wider growth initiatives.
* Conduct consultative discovery calls to understand how prospective customers currently identify, assess and manage commercial opportunities.
* Deliver tailored product demonstrations based on each prospect’s markets, workflows and commercial objectives.
* Build relationships with internal champions, commercial decision-makers and other stakeholders.
* Manage proposals, pilots, negotiations and contract discussions.
* Maintain accurate pipeline records, forecasts and clearly defined next steps.
* Develop outbound strategies for priority accounts, sectors and markets.
* Use modern CRM, prospecting, enrichment and sales intelligence tools to identify and prioritise opportunities.
* Work closely with the product team, sharing customer feedback and market intelligence.
* Support and provide direction to a Sales Development Representative.
* Help shape the company's GTM strategy, refining sales processes, messaging, target markets and commercial playbooks.
* Contribute to future recruitment and the continued development of the sales team.
**Candidate Profile**
We are looking for an entrepreneurial and commercially curious salesperson who is searching for more than another individual contributor role. You may already have some leadership experience, or you could be a successful Account Executive who has mentored colleagues, introduced new processes or led team activity and is now ready to take the next step. Either way, you must remain comfortable with hands-on selling and be motivated by the opportunity to help build a sales function from the ground up.
You will enjoy working autonomously, testing new approaches and taking responsibility for achieving results. You will also be naturally curious about businesses, able to understand different commercial models and confident translating customer challenges into relevant technology-led solutions.
**Key Skills & Experience:**
* Proven experience selling B2B SaaS, software, data or technology solutions.
* A successful track record of owning sales cycles and closing new business.
* Experience creating pipeline through outbound activity rather than relying entirely on inbound leads.
* Confidence conducting discovery calls and delivering software product demonstrations.
* Strong commercial judgement and the ability to quickly understand how different businesses operate.
* Experience navigating multiple stakeholders throughout a sales process.
* Familiarity with modern go-to-market tools, including CRM, prospecting, sequencing, enrichment and sales intelligence platforms.
* The ability to introduce structure, improve processes and contribute to the development of an emerging sales function.
* A hands-on, self-starting approach with high levels of ownership and accountability.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* The confidence to operate effectively within a fast-moving startup environment where the sales playbook is still being developed.
* *Candidates must have a **permanent and unrestricted Right to Work in the UK**, residing within a **commutable distance of Leeds**. Please note that our client **cannot offer visa sponsorship**.*
*Experience within an early-stage SaaS business or selling market intelligence, company data, workflow or sales intelligence software would be advantageous. An understanding of financial services, M&A, private equity, professional services or other data-intensive markets would also be beneficial, although this is not essential.*
**Our Client**
Our client is an early-stage AI SaaS business developing an innovative platform that brings company discovery, market intelligence, contact data, commercial signals and pipeline workflows together in one place. The platform helps B2B teams identify which organisations to target, understand why they represent a relevant opportunity, find the right people to approach and collaborate around a shared commercial pipeline. Following early investment and customer growth, the business is now developing its commercial function and preparing for its next phase of growth.

The Manufacturing Engineer role at IMI Process Automation is a full-time position in Poole, Dorset. The work covers process development, new-product introduction, production handover, assembly, testing, tooling, and continuous improvement.
IMI Process Automation makes highly engineered fluid and motion-control products for industrial automation, process automation, climate control, life science, fluid control, and transport applications. The position works across Design Engineering, R&D, Production Engineering, Quality, Projects, Manufacturing, Operations, and Quality Engineering. Applicants need an engineering degree in mechanical, manufacturing, production engineering, or a related subject, or equivalent qualifications and experience. Apply For This Role
An applicant has a CV or resume, a current email address, and a phone number ready before completing the online application.
## Process Development And Production Handover
The engineer develops, proves, and improves manufacturing methods, workflows, and production processes. New-product introduction work connects design intent with repeatable assembly and testing, while production handover turns an approved design into controlled shop-floor activity. Feasibility studies, production trials, pilot builds, and pre-production runs form part of the engineering assignment.
The engineer analyses production performance to identify process problems that need structured investigation. Lean improvement work includes 5S, Kaizen, SMED, and error-proofing. The engineer also introduces new equipment and technologies, commissions production equipment, and provides technical support during live manufacturing.
## Tooling, Risk And Quality Controls
The engineer develops fixtures, jigs, test rigs, assembly aids, and other equipment that supports consistent production. The engineer works with Quality Engineering to define inspection and validation requirements before a process moves into routine manufacture. Welding procedures and qualification records form part of the technical documentation when the manufacturing route requires them.
* Manufacturing risk assessments and PFMEAs
* Process capability studies
* Engineering drawings and design-intent reviews
* Routes, standard operating procedures, work instructions, and training materials
* ERP and MRP production data
Operators follow defined methods, inspection points, and training content in the manufacturing documentation. The records connect each production decision to evidence that production and quality teams can use.
## Engineering Knowledge And Digital Tools
The technical work requires knowledge of manufacturing processes, assembly techniques, engineering materials, and first-principles calculations. Three-dimensional printing and additive manufacturing are included in the expected technical range. Autodesk, product lifecycle management systems, Microsoft Office, and other PC-based systems support the design, planning, and production records.
High-pressure valve experience in nuclear, oil and gas, or space applications is desirable for the role. Relevant certification, customer practices, and regulations add value in those environments. Electrical engineering, automation, and solenoid design knowledge are additional desirable skills for the fluid-control products made by the business.
## Poole's Critical-Engineering Facility
The Poole manufacturing team works within IMI's Dorset operation. A purpose-built IMI Poole facility covers 105,000 square feet at Technology Road industrial park. The site replaced IMI's former Creekmoor location and was planned as a centre of engineering excellence for critical applications.
The Poole operation includes IMI Herion, IMI Maxseal, and IMI Thompson Valves. The facility makes high-integrity solenoid valves, pressure regulators, and other industrial components, with local capacity for products from other IMI businesses. Energy, chemical, and marine industries are among the sectors connected with the Dorset manufacturing work.
## Scope Of The Engineering Assignment
The engineer owns manufacturing-development tasks within an agreed scope and manages priorities independently. Strong analysis, problem-solving, organisation, communication, cross-functional teamwork, and attention to detail support that responsibility. Senior or lead engineers handle escalation and final approvals, giving the role a defined route for technical decisions that exceed its assigned scope.
Day-to-day decisions connect product requirements with production methods, equipment, records, and operator training. The engineer combines hands-on process work with written engineering control, allowing a new or revised product to move through trials, validation, and production with its technical evidence intact.

Managers across a council operate in different settings, so advice must translate into daily practice. The role supports managers to understand their responsibilities, take ownership of risk and use learning to prevent repeat problems. The work also strengthens accountability rather than treating safety as a separate administrative exercise.
## Risk Control And Prevention Work
Workplace health and safety management starts with identifying hazards and assessing the risks attached to them. The HSE health and safety guidance also covers planning, monitoring and reviewing control measures, alongside worker information and training.
The role's prevention focus connects policy with operational decisions. A council health and safety team may review arrangements, advise service managers, examine learning from incidents and check that responsibilities are understood. These activities require careful records, clear recommendations and the confidence to challenge weak controls.
* Developing health and safety arrangements
* Advising senior leaders and managers
* Providing assurance on risk management
* Strengthening prevention and organisational learning
* Building everyday management accountability
## Working With Services And Senior Leaders
Advice reaches its value when managers can act on it. The post therefore combines technical health and safety knowledge with communication, prioritisation and the ability to explain risk in terms that service teams can use.
Dorset Council's careers programme covers adult services, children's services, professional and support work, environment and planning, and community and transport. A council-wide manager must recognise that each service has its own work activities while keeping the underlying duties consistent. The organisation's size gives the post a broad internal audience and a substantial range of operational relationships.
## Professional Practice In A Council Setting
Competent health and safety advice includes more than writing policies. It involves helping an employer identify hazards, choose proportionate controls, provide information and training, and review whether arrangements work in practice. The HSE risk management steps describe this cycle in practical terms.
People entering the role need to connect evidence with decisions. A strong recommendation identifies the hazard, explains the exposure, records the control and sets out how the organisation will know whether the control is working. The manager also needs to keep advice understandable for non-specialists who carry responsibility for day-to-day operations.

# Clinical Bioinformatician (we have office locations in Cambridge, Leeds and London)
* Full-time
* Department: Bioinformatics Engineering
* Office: London
## Company Description
Genomics England is a global leader in enabling genomic medicine and research, focused on creating a world where everyone benefits from genomic healthcare. Building on the 100,000 Genomes Project, we support the NHS’s world-first national whole genome sequencing service and run the growing National Genomic Research Library, alongside delivering numerous major genomics initiatives. By connecting research and clinical care at national scale, we enable immediate healthcare benefits and advances for the future.
Our mission is to provide the evidence and digital systems so that by 2035 genomics could play a role in up to half of all healthcare interactions, whilst securing the UK’s position as the best place to discover, prove and benefit from genomic innovations.
We are accelerating our impact and working with patients, doctors, scientists, government and industry to improve genomic testing, and help researchers access the health data and technology they need to make new medical discoveries and create more effective, targeted medicines for everybody.
Behind the Healthcare and Research outcomes, Genomics England delivers through designing, developing and operating complex healthcare software systems.
We're on the cusp of big changes with the real prospect of genomics becoming the fabric of everyday healthcare through the lifetime – from birth to old age.
## Job Description
We are hiring a Clinical Bioinformatician to join our Rare Disease Decision Support System squad, helping shape digital tools that support whole genome sequencing interpretation across the NHS Genomic Medicine Service.
This is a collaborative role where your clinical science, rare disease genomics or bioinformatics expertise will help translate complex genomic information into safe, clear and effective product functionality for clinical users and patients.
You will help define requirements and test scenarios, review designs and functionality, provide clinical guidance and sign-off, and support UAT, documentation, training and ongoing product development.
Initially the role might not require significant amounts of programming or coding, as you will be mostly working alongside a team that includes Engineers and Bioinformatics Engineers. However, we do need someone who is comfortable to write code when called upon and communicate with technical colleagues.
**Everyday responsibilities include:**
* Provide clinical and scientific input into new and existing Rare Disease DSS functionality.
* Work closely with Product Managers, Designers, Engineers, QA, Clinical Safety and Genomic Data Science colleagues to translate clinical needs into clear requirements, user stories and acceptance criteria.
* Review designs, tickets and delivered functionality to ensure they reflect clinical workflows, data limitations, edge cases and potential clinical risks.

Hey! We're team Granola 👋
We're building a category-defining product, backed by a $125M Series C and used daily by teams at companies like Cursor, Vanta, and Linear. We started by making meeting notes better. Now we're turning every conversation a company has into context that people and agents can act on: shared team workspaces, APIs and integrations, and agentic workflows that do something with what was said.
If you haven't already, you should check out what we're building, and why you should work here.
The role
You'll own the systems that make Granola fast, accurate and trustworthy for the next 100x of users, and you'll help decide what's worth building. Our backend engineers talk to users and ship product, not just services.
What you'll work on
The voice pipeline. Scale real-time transcription so notes land accurately in seconds, on every device people use.
New models in production. Evaluate new voice and transcription models as they're released, and get the best ones into users' hands.
The agent harness. Build the harness Granola's agents run in: long-running jobs, tool calls, retries, and retrieving the right context.
APIs and integrations. Extend the APIs and integrations that let people bring Granola context into the AI tools they already use.
Enterprise-grade trust. Build the permissions, data isolation and admin controls that let a company roll Granola out across every team.
Data at scale. Own Postgres performance, observability and alerting as usage grows.
How we work
People and product first. We hire people who are kind, down to earth and pragmatic, who care deeply about the product, and who want to stay connected to the customers using it. Product isn't one team's job here; it's everyone's.
High autonomy. Engineers spot opportunities and ship improvements themselves. We’d rather you ship it than write about it.
Everyone talks to users. Every engineer works directly with the people using Granola, and that's where most of our best ideas come from.
A high bar for engineering and product. We expect strong technical ability and strong product sense. Engineers think like PMs: they understand the user's problem and help shape the direction of what they build.
Room to experiment. Every engineer has a budget from day one to use new models, tools and technologies which make them more productive.
Design and quality matter. Thoughtful design, a high quality bar and close collaboration on everything we build.
We work in person, with flexibility. We’re in the office five days a week because we genuinely like building together. It’s relaxed: dress down, bring your dog, and no fixed office hours.
What that looks like in practice: the version of Granola we use internally goes far beyond the public app. We're building at the frontier of agentic software, and we try every new capability on ourselves first.
The team
The Granola team is kind, curious and design-obsessed. Many of us are former founders, others have built products at Figma, Apple, Google and Meta, and we're all still learning from each other.
Who we're looking for
We don't set a minimum number of years. Some of our strongest engineers graduated two years ago; others have run their own companies. We care about what you've built and how you think about it.
You've owned backend systems in production that real users depended on, and you can talk through the trade-offs you made.
You're strong in TypeScript and Node.js.
You know relational databases deeply (we use Postgres): query plans, indexing, and migrations without downtime.
You're comfortable with cloud infrastructure as code (we use AWS, Terraform and a lot of Lambda).
You think about security and failure modes before the happy path.
You have product sense: you can explain why a system matters to the person using it, and you'd rather ship what users need this week than the perfect version next quarter.
Bonus: experience with speech or audio pipelines, LLM infrastructure, evals, or streaming systems.
Our stack
TypeScript, Node.js, Postgres, AWS (with plenty of Lambda), Terraform, plus whichever new models and tools prove themselves. You don't need experience with everything, but you should be excited to work close to the product and at real scale.
How we hire
Our interviews start with the product: who the user is, what problem matters and what you'd build first. Throughout, we're looking for product sense, good judgement on trade-offs, real engineering depth, and how you'd use your experience to shape a product from the ground up. We also look for people who ship quickly, iterate and love to experiment, and who stay kind and pragmatic along the way.
What we offer
We're living in the most exciting time for tool builders since Engelbart's demo in 1968, and we want to build that future together in London. We pay slightly above market on salary and above market on equity. We work together in person five days a week at our office in Old Street, and we offer relocation support if you're moving to London.

# Staff Power Integrity Engineer
Bristol, UK
**About the job**
Shape the power-delivery architecture behind Graphcore’s high-performance AI compute systems, from voltage regulation through package, PCB and silicon.
As Staff Power Integrity Engineer, you will provide technical leadership on Graphcore’s most complex power-delivery challenges. Your analysis and judgement will directly influence architecture and product decisions.

The Signal and Power Integrity team sits at the centre of Graphcore’s hardware development. We work across disciplines to understand electrical behaviour and guide consequential architecture decisions.

**What we’re looking for**
* Deep practical expertise in power integrity and complex power-delivery network design.
* Strong understanding of PDN impedance, transient behaviour, voltage droop, resonance, stability and decoupling across high-current digital systems.

**Howden Private Capital Due Diligence Graduate Programme**
**Please read before submitting:** You may only apply to **one** graduate programme for our 2027 intake. Submitting duplicate applications will result in them not being considered.
**Location:** London
**Start date:** September 2027
**Salary:** £35,000
**Working structure:** Hybrid
**Due Diligence Graduate Programme**
**Gain Exposure to Live Private Equity and M&A Transactions**
Looking for a graduate role where you'll develop analytical, commercial and problem-solving skills while working on live transactions?
Join Howden Private Capital's Due Diligence team, a newly established global division serving private equity, private credit, infrastructure and institutional investor clients. As a Graduate Analyst, you’ll learn how we support private equity firms, investors and their advisers as they assess and manage risks during acquisitions, investments and corporate transactions.
Our clients are some of the world's leading private equity firms, investors and legal advisers. We help them understand potential insurance and risk exposures before they invest, providing insights that support informed business decisions.
This is a fast-paced, deal-driven environment where no two days are the same. You'll gain exposure to mergers and acquisitions, private equity, risk analysis and client advisory work while building a strong foundation for a long-term career in financial services.
This is a permanent role supported by a structured 18-month development programme, designed to accelerate your professional confidence, technical expertise and career growth.
**What you’ll be doing?**
You'll begin with a structured induction before joining the Due Diligence team, where you'll work alongside experienced specialists on live client projects.
During the programme, you’ll:
* Support insurance due diligence projects for private equity firms, investors and corporate clients.
* Research companies, industries and market trends to support transaction activity.
* Analyse information and identify potential risks associated with acquisitions and investments.
* Assist in preparing client reports, presentations and transaction-related deliverables.
* Support colleagues working on live mergers, acquisitions and investment transactions.
* Work closely with clients, legal advisers and internal stakeholders across Howden.
* Develop an understanding of how insurance and risk management support investment decisions and value creation.
**Who are we looking for?**
**No insurance experience is needed; we’ll teach you everything you need to know!**
**You'll be:**
* A recent graduate, or in your final year of university study.
* Curious, analytical and motivated to learn.
* Interested in business, financial services, private equity, transactions or consulting.
* Able to articulate your points clearly and confidently.
* Someone who enjoys working with others and building relationships.
* Comfortable analysing information and solving problems.
* Organised and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage competing priorities.
* Resilient and adaptable in a fast-paced environment.
* Someone who takes ownership, shows initiative and enjoys asking questions.
* A collaborative team player who enjoys working across different teams and functions.
To be eligible for our programme, you must have the full and unrestricted right to work in the UK.
**Application process**
**Our application process is designed to help you show your potential, not to test what you already know!**
* **Online application form – no CV required:** We believe you're more than just a document, so we won’t ask you to submit a CV. **Please upload a blank document on the application form.**
* **Online gamified assessment:** We’ve created games that will help us understand your natural strengths and how you approach different situations. There are no right or wrong answers. You can complete this stage on your phone or laptop, whichever suits you best!
* **Pre-recorded video interview:** You will record your answers to a few questions using your phone or laptop, giving you the chance to tell us more about yourself in your own time in a relaxed setting.
* **Assessment centre:** Our final stage is an in-person assessment centre at one of our offices. You'll take part in some fun group activities and meet our team in a relaxed setting. This day is all about getting to know you better and for you to see what it's like to be part of Howden and experience our culture. We'll cover all your travel costs for this day, because where you are now, shouldn’t hold back your future!
**Why should you apply?**
At Howden, people are at the heart of everything we do. As an employee-owned business, we believe success is built through collaboration, learning and supporting one another. You'll join a permanent role from day one and take part in our structured 18-month development programme, designed to accelerate your technical, commercial and professional growth.
You'll also benefit from:
* A starting salary of £35,000 and a generous pension scheme.
* Opportunity to complete fully funded professional qualifications, such as the CII or CFA, to support your long-term career development.
* Structured learning and development through our 18-month graduate development programme.

## Lead and shape Huel’s global logistics network across the UK and US, building a smarter, scalable operation that keeps products moving, customers happy and supports our next phase of growth.
We usually respond within two weeks
**Hey! We're Huel, and we're pleased to meet you 👋**
Our culture thrives on high performance, and we set the bar high for new Hueligans who join us.
We invite you to read the advert below for our new **Head of Logistics** position to understand the role, and explore our 7 Huel values before applying to ensure we have the right working environment for you!
### The role
Getting our products to customers reliably, quickly and cost-effectively is fundamental to Huel’s reputation and growth. As we continue to scale rapidly across our DTC, Retail & Amazon channels in the UK, EU and US, we need our logistics and freight operations to keep up with the pace - running smoothly day to day while evolving to support the next phase of the business in the most efficient way. That’s where our new Head of Logistics comes in to lead this critical function.
The logistics team is based within our wider Operations function. No day is ever the same, but here’s an insight into what you can expect:
* Hold overall accountability for our outbound logistics and warehousing operations across the UK and US, ensuring reliable, cost-effective fulfilment that protects customer availability and service levels across all sales channels.
* Own our inbound freight operation - the movement of raw materials and finished goods around the world, the majority of which is container shipment - working closely with Sourcing and Product Supply to keep the supply chain flowing.
* Manage our 3PL and freight partners to continually improve service, quality and cost, setting clear performance expectations and KPIs, holding partners to account and building strong operational relationships.
* Develop the automation and network strategy for our next phase of growth with our 3PL logistics partners in the UK and US, including CAPEX cases and payback analysis, and lead delivery of agreed initiatives.
* Continuously identify and deliver cost, efficiency and service improvements across the network - from carrier and route optimisation to warehouse operations and freight consolidation - ensuring Huel is always getting a great deal.
* Ensure full compliance with customs, import/export and trade requirements across our UK, EU and US operations, managing risk through robust systems and processes.
* Lead our Customer Supply teams across the UK and US, with overall accountability for order management and fulfilment to our retail and marketplace customers, and operational relationships with key customers’ supply chain teams.
* Own logistics and customer service KPIs across all channels, working with Commercial, Product Supply and Finance to resolve issues quickly and ensure financial forecasts accurately reflect logistics requirements.
* Lead logistics capacity planning as part of our S&OP process, ensuring our logistics footprint and partner capacity can keep pace with Huel’s growth, new markets and channel expansion, with logistics requirements built into expansion initiatives from the outset.
* Lead, coach and develop a team of c.12 across the UK and US, providing clear direction, structure and inspiration while empowering autonomy across the team.
Not yet sure if this is the right role for you? Click **HERE**to read a more detailed job description.
### What we're looking for in you
This role will best suit someone with 10+ years of experience in logistics, distribution and freight within the FMCG sector or a comparable fast-moving, physical-goods environment. You should also have:
* Deep operational knowledge of order picking, warehousing, transport, outbound distribution and international freight (including container shipping, customs and import/export), across DTC, Retail & Amazon fulfilment.
* Proven experience managing 3PL and freight partners - selecting them, setting them up, holding them to account on service, cost and quality, and building strong long-term relationships.
* Robust numerical and financial modelling skills, with the ability to build CAPEX and payback cases for significant investment and present data-driven recommendations simply to senior stakeholders and at board level.
* Experience leading customer supply, order management or customer service teams in FMCG, with a track record of delivering service levels such as OTIF with major retailers and marketplaces.
* A strategic thinker as well as a strong operator - able to run a reliable operation today while shaping how the network scales and automates for the future.
* Deep experience of line management, leadership, coaching and development for a team of varying skill sets across multiple geographies.
* Strong communication and collaboration skills, able to tie together the activities of diverse teams within your remit and partner effectively across the wider Operations function, Sourcing, Product Supply and Commercial.
* Extremely organised, calm and decisive under pressure, with the ability to deal with ambiguity, take responsibility and get the job done in a fast-paced environment, with a passion for change and continuous improvement.
And as always, we’re on the lookout for new Hueligans who love a fast-paced environment and are always striving to be their best. We want people who aren’t afraid to think differently and push boundaries. If you’re all about setting big goals and believe that amazing things happen through creativity and teamwork, you’ll fit right in at Huel!

We know that at times, our teams face demanding pressures, and exceptional effort deserves meaningful rewards. That's why we've created a world-class perks and benefits program designed to support our Hueligans in achieving their best, both professionally and personally, while celebrating the global impact they're making!

**THE NATIONAL POLICE CHIEFS’ COUNCIL (NPCC)**
Policing is operating in a time of global change and uncertainty, the public and our staff need a service which is responsive, able to tackle future challenges and embrace opportunity.
The National Police Chiefs’ Council (NPCC) brings UK police leaders together to set direction in policing and drive progress for the public.
We achieve this through:
* Coordination – by joining up the operational response to critical national policing issues to deliver policing today and shape the future.
* Collaboration – by working in partnership as part of the whole policing system and beyond to improve public safety.
* Communication – by sharing the collective expertise, views and action of UK police chiefs.
**NPCC HYDRANT PROGRAMME**
The Hydrant Programme is a national policing programme supporting the work of the National Police Chiefs’ Council (NPCC) Child Protection and Abuse Investigation Working Group. Originally established in 2014 to coordinate the response to non-recent child sexual abuse but now supporting forces across all child protection and abuse investigation issues.
Hydrant develops policy and strategy on behalf of the NPCC, develops and delivers best practice advice including a learning, review and improvement function, provides a strategic analysis capability and partnership engagement with key stakeholders and partners.
**THE ROLE**
To work within the Hydrant Programme Analysis and Research Team to deliver evidence based, high quality, insightful analysis to support the delivery of national policing response to Group Based Child Sexual Exploitation (CSE)/Child Sexual & Abuse Exploitation (CSAE).
As a Data Analyst, you will be a key member of an agile national multi-disciplinary analytics team, collaborating with Analysts, to initially model and deliver large data sets and assist in analytical reports. A focus on modelling data in its rawest form, ensuring data/statistics are accurate and suitable to meet the reporting requirements of the Hydrant Programme thematic and its stakeholders by utilising a variety of applications to deliver the informative outcomes alongside in-depth insight.
The successful candidate would need to have the following experiences and skills:
* BSc in Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics (STEM) subject OR equivalent practical experience in data analysis or related field.
* An understanding of Python/Java/Scala or other programming languages or statistical/Machine Learning or working in an Agile team using Version control
* Provide the business with accurate, relevant and timely data, research and performance information that contributes to required frameworks and a culture of continuous improvement, enhanced efficiency and evidence-based decision-making in the police.
* Experience of or commitment to learn Structured Query Language (SQL) to be able to write and optimize Structured Query Language (SQL) queries to extract and manipulate data from relational and/or POLE (Person, Object, Location, Event) databases, ensuring data accuracy and integrity.
* Create meaningful and engaging reports and dashboards, using tools such as Power Business Intelligence (PowerBI) and visualisations to effectively communicate data analysis results to non-technical stakeholders.

**Job Description**
# **So, who are we?**
IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and
proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in established businesses.
The bar is high – bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we'll give you the
platform to define what comes next.
Join us at IG – the future gets built here.
## **About the Team**
This role sits within our Conversational AI team, which builds and runs the AI assistant our clients talk to. Quality is what gives the business confidence those standards are being met in every conversation the assistant has, and that we are doing right by our clients and our regulators.
## **Your Role within the Team:**
Our Conversational AI team is building a dedicated quality capability for the bot - new framework, new standards, and AI-assisted tooling - and you will join as we do it. This is a graduate role, and a rare chance to join an AI capability while it is still being shaped rather than after the decisions have all been made. Your core job is to assess real conversations between clients and our AI assistant, judge them fairly and accurately against our quality and conduct standards, and turn what you find into insight the team and our CX colleagues can act on.
Conversational AI lets us answer far more client queries, faster and around the clock, than human agents alone ever could. But an AI assistant can be wrong with complete confidence, and at scale a single flaw in its knowledge, logic, or guardrails can repeat across thousands of conversations before anyone notices. In a regulated business, that is a conduct risk, not just a service one. QA is how we make sure the bot's answers are accurate, compliant, and genuinely helpful, that it knows when to hand a client over to a human, and that it keeps getting better as our client base grows.
You will not just be checking the bot's work. As you build your expertise, you will have the opportunity to get involved in the wider AI projects that make it better - from testing new features and models to helping design how we measure AI quality in the first place. No prior experience in QA or financial services is needed: we will give you full training and support. What we are looking for is curiosity, sharp judgement, and a genuine interest in how AI behaves in the real world.
## ## ## **What You'll Do:**
**Quality evaluations of AI assistant conversations**
* Review client conversations with our AI assistant across chat and other digital channels, scoring them fairly and consistently against a bot-specific evaluation framework.
* Assess the things that matter most: whether the bot understood what the client was actually asking, whether its answer was accurate and grounded in approved content, whether it resolved the query or routed it appropriately, the clarity and tone of its responses, and - critically - whether the conversation met our conduct and regulatory standards.
* Scrutinise handoffs to human agents: whether the bot escalated when it should have, avoided escalating when it did not need to, and passed the client over with enough context that they did not have to start again.
* Use sampling, AI-assisted scoring, and conversation analytics to focus your review where it adds the most value, applying our quality standards consistently and in line with how human interactions are assessed.
**Regulation and Consumer Duty at the centre**
* Treat bot QA as what it is: a core line of defence for regulatory compliance, not a box-ticking exercise. The same standards apply whether a client is served by a person or a machine.
* Identify conduct risk in bot responses - anything that strays into investment advice or a personal recommendation, unbalanced representation of risk and reward, inaccurate or invented information about products, fees, or margin, market abuse indicators, and mishandling of personal data or DSAR requests - and flag it correctly.
* Pay particular attention to Consumer Duty obligations, especially whether the bot recognises expressions of dissatisfaction as complaints, picks up signs of client vulnerability, and routes those clients to a human with appropriate care.
**Testing, investigation and root cause**
* Carry out root cause analysis on failed conversations, DSATs, and other negative outcomes, working out whether the problem sits in intent recognition, the knowledge base, conversation design, the model's behaviour, or the handoff process.
* Look for patterns across conversation types, intents, and topics rather than treating every failure as a one-off, and surface them clearly.
* Help design and run test scenarios - including edge cases and adversarial prompts - to probe how the bot behaves before and after changes, and check that fixes work without breaking something else.undefined
**Feedback that drives improvement**
* Share clear, evidence-based findings that the rest of the Conversational AI team and our product and knowledge colleagues can actually use - with example transcripts, the standard that was missed, and what good would have looked like.Learn to stand behind your assessments.
* Not everyone will agree that a response was a failure, and you will build the confidence to make your case with evidence - and the judgement to concede when the evidence points the other way.
* Connect what you see in evaluations to the bigger picture, feeding insight into content updates, conversation design, guardrails, and release decisions so that the bot's quality improves over time, not just gets measured.undefined
**Getting involved in wider AI projects**
* Get hands-on with AI improvement work beyond day-to-day QA - for example testing new bot features, knowledge content, or model updates before they reach clients.
* Contribute to how we measure AI quality: helping build evaluation datasets, refine scoring criteria, and explore how automated evaluation can work alongside human review.
* Work closely with colleagues across the Conversational AI team and with product, data, and compliance, seeing first-hand how a regulated business builds and governs AI - experience that opens doors across the business.
## **What You'll Need:**
**Essential**
* A degree in any discipline. We are as interested in graduates from psychology, linguistics, law, or philosophy as from computer science, maths, or economics.
* A genuine interest in AI and how it behaves in the real world - you are the kind of person who has poked at a chatbot to see where it breaks and wondered why.
* Excellent written English with a strong grasp of spelling, punctuation and grammar (SPAG). You will be judging the clarity, accuracy, and tone of the bot's written responses, so your own writing needs to be sound.
* A genuinely customer-centric mindset: you can tell the difference between a conversation that technically answered the question and one that actually served the client well.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the curiosity to dig into why the bot responded the way it did rather than simply recording that it got it wrong.
* Attention to detail and consistency. The credibility of QA rests on evaluations being fair, accurate, and defensible.The confidence to share honest, constructive views - or the drive to build that confidence quickly with support.
* An interest in financial services and why regulation matters. You do not need prior knowledge of Consumer Duty or conduct rules - we will teach you - but you should want to understand why they exist.
**Desirable**
* An internship, placement, or part-time role in customer service, compliance, data, or a regulated environment such as financial services.
* Hands-on experience with AI or large language model (LLM) tools, for example through a dissertation, university project, hackathon, or personal project.
* A second language. While not a requirement, the ability to evaluate bot conversations in languages other than English would be a real asset given our global client base.
* Some exposure to data analysis or basic coding (Excel, SQL, or Python) - useful for spotting patterns across large volumes of conversations, but not essential.
* An understanding of research methods, experiment design, or how to measure quality or accuracy in a structured way.
**Your First Few Months:**
* You cannot fairly judge work you have never done yourself, so you will start by going through our CX agent training. You will learn our products, systems, and processes from the agent's seat and get a real feel for what a good client interaction looks like in practice. You will then spend time across the Conversational AI team to understand how the bot is built, what it is and is not allowed to do, and how changes to it are made. Throughout, you will have a dedicated mentor in the team and structured training on financial services regulation and Consumer Duty. From there, you will ramp into the role itself:
* **First**, getting to know our bot evaluation framework and tooling inside out, and completing evaluations under guidance until you are scoring fairly and consistently.
* **Then**, carrying out root cause analysis on failed conversations independently, contributing to test scenarios, and presenting your findings to the wider team and our CX colleagues.
* **In time**, taking on a role in wider AI projects, spotting the patterns and conduct risks others miss, and helping shape how the bot is improved and what gets tested next.
## **What's in It for You:**
* A front-row seat in conversational AI at a FTSE 100 FinTech, with real responsibility from the start.Structured training in QA, financial services regulation, and AI evaluation, plus a dedicated mentor.
* Exposure to wider AI projects and cross-functional teams, and a foundation to grow into QA, AI quality, conversation design, or product roles as your interests develop.
## **The perks:**
It really is more than a job. We think like a start-up, but we deliver like a FTSE 100 — so the bar is high, and we won't pretend otherwise. We work hybrid, which means three days in the office. We’ll recognise your talent and make sure that you can still have a life – at work, and outside of it. ## Principal Platform & Infrastructure Engineer
**Job no:** 502913 **Work type:** Experienced Professional **Location:** Kings Langley UK, Bristol UK **Categories:** Graphics ### **The role**
We are building a modern orchestration platform to replace a legacy system of ad-hoc scripts that coordinate long-running, resource-intensive compute jobs across on-premises HPC/HTC infrastructure and cloud environments. The platform must give engineers clear visibility into multi-day job pipelines, respond intelligently to failures, and scale compute capacity elastically between on-prem hardware and the cloud during peak demand.
This is a foundational, greenfield build. You will be the senior-most voice on infrastructure, security, and platform architecture, working closely with a software/application engineer who owns the orchestration logic and application-layer design. You'll set the technical direction for how the platform is deployed, secured, and operated — establishing patterns the rest of the team will follow, rather than discovering them through trial and error.
We are intentionally vague here about the specific domain and tooling; the technical depth and architectural challenges are what matter, and we'll cover the specifics in interview.
You will:
* Own the end-to-end platform architecture: from bare-metal/hypervisor layer through networking, cloud, and orchestration infrastructure.
* Design and implement the on-prem virtualization layer (e.g. Proxmox or equivalent) supporting compute clusters, control-plane services, and developer/test environments.
* Design hybrid cloud architecture (primarily Azure) including compute bursting strategy, cost controls, and workload placement between on-prem and cloud.
* Architect network topology: subnet design, VLAN segmentation, firewall rules, DMZ boundaries, and secure ingress/egress between on-prem HPC/HTC resources, cloud environments, and external services.
* Design and implement identity, authentication, and authorization: RBAC models, service accounts, SSO/federation, least-privilege access policies across platform components.
* Own secrets management strategy (e.g. Vault, Azure Key Vault, or equivalent) and ensure secrets are never hard-coded or leaked into logs/artifacts.
* Build and maintain Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform) and configuration management (Ansible) to make environment provisioning repeatable, auditable, and version-controlled.
* Define and enforce security baselines: patching cadence, vulnerability scanning, network hardening, audit logging.
* Partner with the application development lead to define clean interfaces between infrastructure concerns (deployment, secrets, networking) and application logic (workflow/task design).
* Act as a technical mentor across the team on infrastructure and security topics — you are expected to unblock others quickly by applying established patterns, not by re-deriving them from scratch.
* Participate in incident response and capacity planning for production workloads.
* Evaluate and make build-vs-buy decisions for infrastructure tooling.
### **About you**
Committed to making your customers, stakeholders and colleagues successful, you’re an excellent communicator, listener and collaborator who builds trusted partnerships by delivering what you say, when you say. You’re curious, solutions orientated and a world-class problem solver who constantly seeks opportunities to innovate and achieve the best possible outcome to the highest imaginable standard.
You will have:
* Extensive experience in infrastructure/platform engineering, with demonstrable ownership of production systems end-to-end.
* Deep hands-on experience with on-prem virtualization from bare metal (e.g. Proxmox, VMware, or similar hypervisor platforms) — not just cloud-only experience.
* Strong production experience with Azure (compute, networking, IAM, storage); familiarity with hybrid/multi-cloud patterns.
* Solid networking fundamentals: subnetting, VLANs, routing, firewall design, DMZ architecture, VPN/site-to-site connectivity.
* Practical experience designing and implementing RBAC, authentication/authorization systems (OAuth2/OIDC, SAML, service principals), and secrets management platforms (Vault, Key Vault, or similar).
* Strong Terraform experience (modules, state management, multi-environment patterns) and Ansible (or equivalent configuration management) for provisioning and configuration.
* Comfortable working in Linux-centric environments; strong shell scripting ability.
* Experience securing systems that bridge on-prem and cloud boundaries (e.g. HPC/HTC compute farms, hybrid data planes).
* Understanding of container runtimes (Docker and/or HPC/HTC-oriented alternatives like Apptainer/Singularity) and their networking/security implications.
You might also have:
* Experience with Kubernetes for cloud-burst or elastic compute scenarios.
* Familiarity with workflow orchestration tools (e.g. Prefect, Airflow, Dagster) — not required to design flows, but useful for understanding deployment/runtime needs.
* Exposure to high-performance/scientific/technical computing environments (HPC/HTC schedulers, license-managed software, compute farms).
* Experience with observability stacks (Prometheus/Grafana, ELK, or equivalent).
* Prior experience in a regulated or IP-sensitive industry where security posture is critical.
