As Head of Technical Account Management for Europe, the Middle East, and Africa (EMEA), you will own the regional direction and performance of TAMSS, including teams supporting Stripe’s largest direct merchants and platforms.
You’ll translate Stripe’s global priorities into regional plans that reflect EMEA’s markets, users, and commercial opportunities. Your remit will include user outcomes, service quality, paid support growth, organizational health, and the effective allocation of TAM capacity.
You’ll also serve as an executive partner for strategically important users and represent EMEA on the global TAMSS leadership team. Insights from the region will inform how Stripe develops its products, services, and approach to supporting complex users around the world.
**Responsibilities**
* Set and execute the multi-year strategy and operating model for EMEA TAMSS.
* Lead and scale a substantial, distributed EMEA Technical Account Management organization, developing a strong management layer across multiple markets, user segments, and technical domains.
* Own regional outcomes across paid support growth, service delivery, strategic-user health, technical impact, and organizational performance.
* Determine the regional organization and coverage model, including leadership structure, market coverage, capacity allocation, and investment priorities.
* Partner with senior leaders across Sales, Customer Success, Product, Engineering, Support, Professional Services, and Solutions Architecture to deliver coordinated outcomes for users.
* Work with go-to-market leaders on paid support adoption, renewals, account strategy, staffing, and the sustainable growth of Stripe’s services business.
* Build trusted relationships with executive technical and business leaders at Stripe’s largest users, serving as a senior escalation point when needed.
* Provide executive oversight for high-impact user escalations and critical support incidents, ensuring clear ownership, rapid coordination, timely communication, and effective resolution, translating learnings into support experience improvements.
* Use user feedback, commercial insights, and operational data to identify risks, improve performance, and inform investment decisions.
* Turn patterns from complex user engagements into improvements to Stripe’s products, services, and operating models.
* Hire and develop managers, set clear expectations, and build a strong succession pipeline for critical leadership roles.
* Represent EMEA in global TAMSS planning and develop approaches that can be adopted across other regions.
## Who you are
We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

* 15+ years of experience in technical account management, solutions architecture, customer success, or related user-facing technical functions, including 6+ years managing people and experience managing managers.
* A track record of leading substantial, distributed organizations through multiple organizational layers, developing managers, and retaining strong management and technical talent.
* Experience setting multi-year strategy and translating it into organizational plans, investment decisions, and measurable user and business outcomes.
* Experience building trusted relationships with executive business and technical leaders at large and strategically important users.
* Strong technical and commercial judgment, including the ability to understand complex integrations, assess user and service-delivery risks, and work effectively with Product and Engineering leaders.
* Demonstrated success aligning senior leaders with different priorities around a shared strategy.
**Preferred qualifications**
* Experience with P&L management, budget ownership, or operating in a General Manager (GM) capacity for a regional services organization.
* Experience leading a technical services organization across multiple EMEA markets.

* Experience in financial technology, payments, Software as a Service, or API-based products.

Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. Also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible.

The annual salary range for this role in the primary location is €150,400 - €225,600. This range may change if you are hired in another location. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings (“OTE”) range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the primary location may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.
Specific benefits and details about what compensation is included in the salary range listed above will vary depending on the applicant’s location and can be discussed in more detail during the interview process. Benefits/additional compensation for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; retirement plans; health benefits; and wellness stipends.

Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

**Are you a Finance leader who knows what “good” looks like — and has the experience and personality to make it happen?**
We’re looking for a **Head of Finance** to join Pro-Pak Foods in Malton and play a key role in shaping the next stage of our Finance function.
This isn’t a role for someone who simply wants to produce the numbers and move on.
We’re looking for someone who wants to **understand what sits behind the numbers, ask the difficult questions, find the answers and use financial information to genuinely improve the business.**
Ideally, you’ll come from a **food manufacturing environment** and have already experienced what a strong, well-run Finance function looks like. Perhaps you’ve done it before — and now you’re looking for the opportunity to do it again, with the autonomy to make a real difference.
**What will you be doing?**
As Head of Finance, you’ll take ownership of the day-to-day running and development of our **Finance & Business Administration teams**, providing strong financial leadership across the site.
You’ll be responsible for ensuring the business has **accurate, timely and meaningful financial information**, whilst maintaining robust financial controls and supporting the delivery of our commercial and operational strategy.
**Your responsibilities will include:**
* Leading, developing and empowering the Finance team, creating a more dynamic and forward-thinking function.
* Providing clear financial leadership and ensuring colleagues are engaged, developed and performing at their best.
* Producing weekly and monthly financial reporting, including **P&L, Balance Sheet and Cash Flow** information.
* Owning the annual budgeting process and quarterly reforecasts.
* Providing regular and ad hoc **cost centre analysis**, including investigation of variances against budget and standards.
* Making sure Finance doesn't simply report variances — **we understand why they happened and what needs to happen next.**
* Maintaining strong financial processes, controls and reconciliations, ensuring audit and legislative requirements are met.
* Overseeing balance sheet reconciliations, accruals, prepayments, fixed assets and other core accounting processes.
* Supporting CAPEX and ICO processes.
* Driving cost reduction opportunities and commercial improvements across the site.
* Monitoring departmental KPIs and challenging performance where improvement is required.
* Developing systems, processes and reporting to make Finance more structured, efficient and useful to the wider business.
* Working closely with the leadership team, internal departments, Group/Premium Foods Group and external auditors.
* Providing financial insight that helps turn data into **meaningful actions and better decisions.**
* Supporting national statistics and monthly survey requirements.
* Championing best practice across Finance and the wider business.
**More importantly, what are we looking for?**
* We’re looking for someone who **knows Finance inside out — but also knows how a business works.**
* Demonstrable experience leading a Finance function or team, preferably within **food manufacturing or a similar FMCG environment**.
* AAT, CIMA, ACCA or equivalent qualification.
* Experience of working in a business where Finance is expected to **explain the numbers, not just produce them**.
* A strong understanding of what a good Finance function looks like — and ideally evidence that you've built or operated one before.
* The confidence to **challenge when required**. If information isn't available, you'll ask for it. If something doesn't make sense, you'll investigate it. If an explanation isn't good enough, you'll keep asking questions.
* The ability to turn existing processes and information into **more structured systems, reports and ways of working**.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills — including the ability to work things out when the answer isn't immediately available.
* Advanced Excel and data-analysis skills.
* Excellent organisation and attention to detail.
* Strong commercial awareness, with experience identifying and delivering cost-saving opportunities.
* The ability to work autonomously, make sound decisions and bring issues through to a conclusion.
* Experience developing and motivating teams and getting the best out of people.
* Strong communication skills and the confidence to work with stakeholders at all levels.
**And the bit that doesn't appear on a Finance qualification...**
* We want someone who's good to work with. You'll be someone we can rely on.
* Someone who can be trusted to get stuck into a problem rather than wait for someone else to solve it.
* Someone who can have a robust conversation when necessary, but who also knows how to build relationships and bring people with them.
* Someone who's **structured, forward-thinking and commercially minded**, but doesn't take themselves too seriously.
* A good sense of humour would be very welcome.
* You’ll have significant autonomy in the role, but you’ll also be a key member of the wider senior leadership team — so being **personable, approachable and collaborative** really matters.
**What does success look like?**
* Over time, we want Finance to become **more structured, more proactive and more commercially valuable to the business**.
* We want better reporting, better systems, better answers and better insight.

## **Role Overview**
As the Head of IT & Infrastructure, you will have end-to-end ownership of Red Badger’s global IT landscape. This is a dynamic, high-impact role that blends strategic leadership with hands-on execution. You will ensure our multi-location staff enjoy frictionless, secure, and reliable technology experiences every day.
You will manage our identity stack, cloud networking, SaaS ecosystem, device fleet, and compliance standards (ISO 27001 & Cyber Essentials) across our four hubs (London, Leeds, Cape Town, and Australia & New Zealand). As Red Badger grows, you will build and lead a distributed IT team, travelling to regional hubs when necessary to establish local infrastructure.
## **Key Responsibilities**
#### **1. Global Infrastructure, Identity & Access Management**
* Administer, optimise, and secure our cloud-first identity and access ecosystem, centered around Google Workspace and JumpCloud.
* Implement and enforce modern zero-trust architecture, maintaining Single Sign-On (SSO) and SCIM provisioning across all company applications.
* Manage, maintain, and upgrade physical networks across all locations, including firewalls, Wi-Fi infrastructure, and cloud RADIUS setup.
#### **2. SaaS Ecosystem & Vendor Management**
* Act as the commercial and administrative owner for Red Badger’s SaaS stack (100+ applications).
* Oversee license management, vendor renewals, billing optimization, and procurement to ensure cost efficiency and compliance.
#### **3. User Support, AV & Daily Operations**
* Provide high-touch 1st-line and escalated support to all Red Badger staff across time zones (London, Leeds, Cape Town, Australia & New Zealand).
* Administer and maintain office Audio-Visual systems, specifically Google Meet Hardware rooms, ensuring seamless hybrid collaboration.
* Establish IT onboarding/offboarding workflows that guarantee day-one readiness for new hires worldwide.
#### **4. Device Fleet Management (MDM)**
* Manage the full lifecycle of Red Badger's endpoint fleet (laptops and mobile devices), including procurement, deployment, patch management, security policy enforcement, and eco-friendly disposal via MDM tools.
#### **5. Governance, Security & Compliance**
* Lead, gain, and maintain key industry certifications, including Cyber Essentials / Cyber Essentials Plus and ISO 27001.
* Take responsibility for ensuring data retention policies are in place and align to current legislation.
* Conduct regular security audits, vulnerability assessments, and access reviews across all systems.
* Create, update, and enforce IT security policies and disaster recovery procedures.
#### **6. Global Growth & Team Leadership**
* Support business growth in regional hubs (Leeds, Cape Town, Australia & New Zealand) by defining local IT setups and travelling on-site during initial rollouts or expansions.

Do you believe in the power of data to improve people’s lives? Do you want to enable exciting data driven research to take place securely and for the public good? Research Data Scotland needs you!

We’re delivering an exciting programme of cross-organisational driver projects funded by the UK Government (Health Data Research Service)– and we’re looking for a Project Manager to be part of it.
## Key details
**Role:** Project Manager **Salary range:** £47,215 - £57,939 per annum **Hours:** 32 per week (Full time - at RDS we offer a four day week for our full-time colleagues) **Location:** Edinburgh (with remote-first ways of working) **Employment type:** Fixed Term Contract (12 months). We are happy to discuss a secondment from similarly minded organisations providing you have prior agreement from your department director or line manager. **Closing date:** 12 October 2026
Find out more and apply
## About us
Research Data Scotland (RDS) is a charity set up by the Scottish public sector and leading universities. We help researchers find and make use of data that can improve the lives of people in Scotland. Working in partnership, we do this by widening the range of data available, creating new data assets and providing a single point of contact for safe, secure and effective access to public data in a trustworthy manner.
Data is often locked away in lots of individual systems, across many different organisations, and isn’t in a format that makes access or integration easy. We can help researchers to unlock the potential of this data by giving them information and advice that speeds up and simplifies their work.
RDS aims to provide a step change in the service to researchers, whilst maintaining the high standards of information governance and data security already in place. We aim to work as openly as possible, maintaining standards in transparency and ethics. Our focus is on providing a streamlined service for researchers, as well as extending the range of data available through the service, particularly in the areas of Covid-19, NHS imaging, geospatial data, children and justice services.
Our partners include Scottish Government, Public Health Scotland, National Records of Scotland (NRS), and the Universities of Aberdeen, Dundee, Edinburgh and Glasgow. We work closely with the national and regional safe havens. And we are in contact with other organisations in Scotland and across the UK in the data research sector, including public sector, research and commercial bodies.
## About the job
RDS is undertaking an exciting co-ordinated programme of work to transform the operating model for data access for research in Scotland, with partners in the Scottish Safe Haven Network.
The Scottish Safe Haven Network covers 5 federated Data Safe Havens. Each Safe Haven node has responsibility for controlling secure and ethical access to patient-level data for scientific and clinical research.
We are looking to recruit an experienced Project Manager to plan, co-ordinate and support the delivery of several driver projects, working closely with colleagues in RDS and across the Scottish Safe Haven Network. The postholder will provide professional project management expertise, build effective relationships and drive progress.
The projects will range from technical aspects of digital enquiry to agreeing a sector wide framework for data governance. Each project will involve some aspect of transformation in data management, technical delivery and/or process support, so knowledge of change management processes would be helpful.
You will work within the established RDS Project Management Framework for managing these projects from concept to conclusion, with collaboration and engagement of Safe Haven Network stakeholders a key feature of the role. This role will also look to learn from projects as they develop and share learnings and disseminate best practice across the whole data landscape.
If you’re excited by innovation, enjoy working in complexity, and want to play a key role in transforming how data is accessed for research, this is a brilliant opportunity to grow your impact and your career.
Applications for secondments from organisations that offer this type of developmental opportunity are welcome.
## About you
You are a credible and curious self-starter. You are highly organised and have proven project management experience, preferably in the public sector or academia. You are passionate about how data driven innovation can transform services and improve wellbeing and have good knowledge of/experience in working with sensitive data and/or secure data platforms.
You’re a confident and adaptable Project Manager who thrives in change and enjoys finding and solving problems. You’re naturally curious, open to new ideas and comfortable challenging the status quo when it leads to better outcomes.
You bring strong relationship‐building skills and know how to bring people with you – whether that’s senior stakeholders, delivery teams or external partners. You communicate clearly, listen well, and can translate complexity into practical, actionable plans.
You’re delivery‐focused, but not rigid. You balance structure with flexibility, using judgement to adapt methodologies and tools to suit the context rather than forcing one‐size‐fits‐all solutions.
Above all, you take ownership, learn from experience, and are motivated by delivering meaningful change that adds real value.
## About the team and ways of working
The Data Team at RDS is made up of experienced data analysts, project managers and data operations specialists with experience across the UK data landscape. RDS is an organisation where you will work in a highly competent and knowledgeable team to forge new ways of getting important data to researchers securely and at scale.
The role will require facilitation of multiple internal and external stakeholders to agree priorities and deliver at pace. In this context curiosity and adaptability are critical skills.
## Life at RDS
We are a small friendly and highly engaged team of people. We promote continuous learning and work hard to build an inclusive and supportive workplace culture. We live our values of integrity, transparency, courage, collaboration and humility.
At RDS we offer a Four Day (32 hours) week for our full-time colleagues, with hybrid working on offer from day one. You can choose to work flexibly from home or use one of our office desks in the Edinburgh Futures Institute. The whole RDS team meets one day per month in-person in Edinburgh or at an off-site away day in the Central Belt. Individual teams organise their own in-person days to collaborate, develop and socialise together.
We offer up to 30 days’ annual leave (including public holidays) and have no set closure days. We have a generous pension and enhanced parental/adoption leave. Our flexible benefits include a Cycle to Work scheme, Dental Insurance and discount vouchers. Our Culture Group helps us seek feedback from colleagues across the organisation to make RDS an even better place to work.

### **Senior Linux Administrator**
Cambridge, UK | Full-time | Permanent | Hybrid Salary: £60,000 to £75,000 + Bonus + Equity

### **About us**
Riverlane’s mission is to master quantum error correction (QEC) and unlock a new age of human progress. From advances in material and climate science, to complex chemistry simulation for new drug design, quantum computers will help humanity solve some of its most important challenges. But without QEC, the industry’s defining technical challenge, such breakthroughs can never be achieved. Riverlane is the world leader in QEC technology. QEC is a complex problem that requires a range of skills, talent and passion. Having raised more than $125M in funding to date to accelerate our cutting-edge R&D in quantum error correction (QEC), Riverlane partners with many of the world’s leading quantum hardware providers and government agencies to make fault-tolerant quantum computing a reality. We’re making remarkable progress and growing fast. ### **About the role**
Riverlane is looking for an experienced Linux administrator to own and grow our core computational infrastructure. This is a hands-on role combining day-to-day administration of our High-Performance Computing (HPC) environment with longer-term planning, automation, and improvement of our infrastructure estate. You'll be the primary owner of our HPC cluster and core Linux infrastructure, working closely with IT management and wider Infrastructure Team to keep systems reliable today while building towards a more resilient, scalable environment for tomorrow.
### **Key Responsibilities**
**HPC Cluster Administration**
* Administer and maintain the HPC cluster, including compute nodes, storage systems, and networking.
* Evaluate and evolve cluster topology, compute node configuration, and hardware resource utilisation as the estate grows.
* Lead the deployment, configuration, and troubleshooting of HPC tooling, particularly Slurm — including queue structures and job scheduling policies.
* Monitor system performance and ensure high availability of HPC resources, using observability tools such as Prometheus; investigate anomalies and outages.
* Assess and maintain the network file storage solution for throughput, scalability, and latency.
**Business As Usual (BAU) Administration**
* Maintain, patch, and troubleshoot core Linux infrastructure (RHEL).
* Act as an escalation point for complex technical issues raised by the Riverlane team.
* Provide operational upkeep of core infrastructure, including servers, tooling, and licence managers.
* Maintain Synopsys EDA tooling, including licence server management, environment configuration, and performance optimisation for electronic design automation workflows.
* Provide sound technical support to users of the HPC environment.
* Improve self-service capability for users, enabling routine tasks (e.g. restarting VNC sessions, resetting passwords) to be performed without engineering intervention.
**Automation & Enhancement**
* Automate routine tasks using scripting and infrastructure-as-code tools (Bash, Python, Ansible).
* Collaborate with the Infrastructure Team to plan and implement improvements to HPC infrastructure.
* Own work packages and deliver them within agreed sprint windows.
* Build and maintain documentation for systems, processes, and configurations.
* Communicate effectively with stakeholders on progress and delivered improvements.
**Security, Compliance & Resilience**
* Ensure security and compliance across the HPC estate, including security hardening and lifecycle management.
* Maintain and develop the off-site backup strategy, ensuring data integrity, disaster recovery readiness, and compliance with data retention policies.
### **Requirements & Experience**
* Extensive experience administering and growing infrastructure in fast-paced engineering environments.
* Enterprise Linux expertise: deep knowledge of Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) administration, security hardening, lifecycle management, and troubleshooting.
* Hands-on experience configuring, scaling, tuning, and troubleshooting job schedulers (e.g. Slurm) and distributed compute environments.
* Strong understanding of network file storage protocols and network optimisation for computational workloads.
* Proficient with container environments and virtualisation infrastructure.
* High proficiency with infrastructure automation tools (Ansible, Python, Bash) and infrastructure-as-code practices.
* Experience with backup and disaster recovery strategy and implementation.
* Experience managing licensed EDA or similar specialist software tooling (e.g. Synopsys) is a strong plus.
* Excellent communication skills, with the ability to support both technical and non-technical users and translate complex issues into clear guidance.

* A comprehensive benefits package that includes an annual bonus plan, private medical insurance, life insurance, and a contributory pension scheme
* Equity, so that our team can share in the long-term success of Riverlane
* 28 days annual leave, plus bank holidays and enhanced family leave
* A diverse work environment that brings together experts in many fields (including software and hardware development, quantum information theory, physics and maths) and over 20 different nationalities
* A learning environment that encourages individual, team and company growth and development, including a regular programme of learning events and training and conference budgets

### **Role Title:** Head of Thermal Hydraulic & Fault Analysis
We are Rolls‐Royce SMR and we’re doing something that’s never been done before. We’re revolutionising an industry. That’s a once‐in‐a‐career opportunity for those excited by such a challenge. This is more than just a job; this is a legacy.
### **About the Team:**
The Performance & Analysis team is the centre of excellence within Rolls‐Royce SMR for the engineering analysis used to substantiate the performance and safety of the power station.
The Thermal Hydraulic & Fault Analysis function is responsible for developing and delivering the analysis methods, tools and evidence that underpin reactor and plant safety. The team provides technical leadership across reactor fault analysis, thermal hydraulic safety assessments, CFD modelling, thermofluid analysis and analysis code validation, supporting both the Generic Design Assessment and future customer programmes.
### **About the Role:**
As Head of Thermal Hydraulic & Fault Analysis, you will provide strategic, technical, programme and functional leadership for all thermal hydraulic analysis activities across the power station.
You will be accountable for the development of analysis methodologies, delivery of reactor and system thermal hydraulic assessments, CFD analysis capability, thermofluid engineering support and code validation programmes. This includes oversight of analysis methods, verification, validation and uncertainty quantification activities, ensuring the organisation can deliver robust and high‐quality technical outputs that support design decisions, safety cases and regulatory engagement.
You will lead a function of approximately 60 engineers, including recognised experts and specialists, while maintaining accountability for the quality, capability and performance of the discipline. The role requires extensive engagement with regulators, customers, industry bodies and senior stakeholders to ensure successful programme delivery and strategic growth of the capability.

# Lead Photonics Design Engineer - III/V Components
Apply for this job
**About us**
Salience Labs is developing optical circuit switching technology for AI infrastructure, aimed at reducing latency and cost in data centre networks. As we move towards deployment, you'll have real ownership of your area and work alongside a highly technical team on a hard problem in AI infrastructure.
**The role**
You'll join a multi-disciplinary research team in the UK to lead the development of III-V active components for integration with silicon photonics. You will take devices from epitaxial stack and device design through fabrication with external partners, to characterisation, reliability and qualification.
**What you'll be doing**
* Lead the design and modelling of III-V active devices, including epitaxial layer structure, gain and power modelling, optical mode design, and electrical and thermal design
* Own the technology roadmap and device specifications for your area, translating system requirements into device design and integration targets
* Lead mask design and tape-outs, including GDS layouts, test structures and design-of-experiment splits
* Manage fabrication runs with external epitaxy and foundry partners: define process flows, review process and in-line data, and resolve yield issues as the technology scales
* Define and lead the characterisation strategy at wafer, chip and integrated-PIC level, including building and automating test setups
* Analyse test data, correlate measured performance with design and process variations, and drive design iterations to close performance gaps
* Work with packaging and reliability engineers on burn-in, accelerated ageing, failure analysis and qualification
* Mentor engineers and, as the team grows, help recruit and develop new team members
**Essential requirements**
* PhD in physics, photonics, electrical engineering, optical engineering or a related subject with 6+ years' relevant experience, or a Master's degree with 8+ years' relevant experience, including at least 4 years' hands-on development of III-V optical amplifiers or semiconductor lasers, preferably in industry
* Proven track record of taking III-V devices from concept through design, fabrication and test, ideally including qualification
* Deep understanding of semiconductor laser and amplifier physics: optical gain, carrier dynamics, quantum-well design, noise, gain saturation and nonlinearities, thermal effects and polarisation dependence
* Hands-on knowledge of III-V epitaxy and fabrication processes (e.g. MOCVD/MBE growth, lithography, etching, passivation, metallisation, facet/AR coating), and experience working with external foundries
* Experience characterising amplifiers or lasers, including optical spectrum analysis, gain and noise measurement, wafer-level probing, temperature-controlled testing and test automation
* Experience with simulation and layout tools for photonic devices, such as Lumerical, Photon Design, Crosslight, RSoft, COMSOL, KLayout, L-Edit or Cadence Virtuoso
* Proven ability to lead technical projects across design, process, test and packaging functions, and experience mentoring or supervising engineers
* Excellent communication skills, critical thinking, attention to detail and self-motivation
**Nice to have**
* Experience integrating III-V active devices with silicon photonics, including coupling design between III-V and silicon waveguides
* Experience line-managing a technical team
* Experience with reliability testing and failure analysis of III-V devices
* Experience developing PDK building blocks or compact models for active devices
* Programming experience (Python, MATLAB or C++) for simulation, test automation and data analysis
* Knowledge of photonic packaging, including fibre coupling, thermal design and TEC control
* A track record of high-quality patents and research papers

We aim to provide excellent investment performance to clients through active management. Established in 1804, we have around 5,500 people across 36 global locations. Schroders' success can be attributed to its diversified business model, spanning different asset classes, client types and geographies.

For Enterprise Data, you will provide architectural leadership across platform integration, interoperability, data access and governance alignment, partnering closely with the Enterprise Data Platform team, which retains ownership of data platform architecture. * Lead the architecture of Cloud Platforms and infrastructure, Developer Platforms, the AI Platform and Superhighway, defining integration, interoperability and data access patterns with Enterprise Data while ensuring alignment with the Data Platform architecture.

* Drive synergy and reuse between the platform pillars through shared patterns, capabilities and standards.
* Provide architectural leadership for AWS and Azure cloud platforms, including infrastructure, security, resilience and governance.
* Guide the architecture of agentic AI capabilities built on Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore, with appropriate security, governance and operational controls.
* Guide the evolution of Superhighway as an agentic-enabled developer platform for professional and citizen developers.
* Partner with Enterprise Data leaders to ensure data architecture and platform capabilities align with the wider technology strategy.
* Build strong relationships with senior stakeholders, architecture teams, engineering teams, security, risk and delivery functions.
* Create and maintain clear architecture documentation, decision records, roadmaps and standards, and drive the agreed vision through to implementation.

* Broad architecture experience across AWS and Azure cloud platforms, including infrastructure, networking, security, resilience and governance.
* Strong understanding of developer platforms and practices, including GitHub, Azure DevOps, CI/CD, infrastructure as code and secure software delivery.
* Understanding of AI platforms and agentic application architectures, ideally including Amazon Bedrock and AgentCore.
* Proven experience shaping platform strategies, reference architectures, architectural principles, standards and multi-year roadmaps.
* Ability to understand complex and competing stakeholder requirements and translate them into coherent architectures and decisions.
* Proven ability to connect multiple technology domains, identify dependencies and drive integration and synergy.
* Strong technical leadership and influencing skills, with the credibility to challenge constructively and gain support for a clear vision.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex architecture clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
* Experience working with senior stakeholders and cross-functional teams in a large, regulated enterprise.
* Strong understanding of security, risk, governance, operational resilience and cost considerations in platform architecture.
* Ability to move between strategic thinking and practical delivery, ensuring architecture supports measurable business and engineering outcomes.
* A collaborative leadership style with the ability to work across organisational boundaries and drive decisions to completion.

A good eye for typography, layout, colour and composition
Experience animating data, charts and infographics clearly and accurately, to client brand guidelines

ShapeBlue is looking for a Junior QA Engineer to help test our infrastructure automation and datacenter optimization tools. # Experiential Marketing Lead (Head of Shopify Spaces, London)
* Remote - United Kingdom
* Creative
## About the role
We believe brand is built in the moments people remember, and few moments stick like being in the room. Events are among the hardest things in marketing to attribute and among the easiest to remember. Nobody decides to start a business because of an ad. They decide because they met someone, heard something, tried something, or saw what was possible up close. We want Shopify to be where that happens.
Shopify is coming to London with its first permanent London Space: a hub for the people turning ideas into companies, side hustles into million-pound brands, and local communities into global commerce movements. On the surface, this will be a beautiful room where Shopify hosts founder talks, product education, retail pop-ups, product launches, and cultural moments. The real job is more interesting: make the Space proof that the future of commerce is already happening here.
Our New York Space has shown what happens when commerce and culture are woven together: 100K+ annual visitors, high-signal brand and creator activations, and moments people keep talking about after they leave, from celebrity-founder pop-ups to tent-pole activations around Marathon Weekend and Fashion Week. London deserves its own version, not a copy/paste of what we have already done. It needs someone with the taste and nerve to make it feel unmistakably of the city.
We’re hiring a Head of Spaces, London to build the experiential program strategy for the Space and run the room: programming, production, community, operations, team, partners, and the culture and quality bar. Your work will help entrepreneurs in London become more successful, make Shopify’s role in retail commerce impossible to miss, and turn the Space into a brand channel that travels far beyond the people who were there in person.
If your instinct is to maximize the calendar, this will be a frustrating role. If your instinct is to ask what people will still be talking about in a month, it will not.
# What you’ll do
* **Build the London strategy for Shopify Spaces.** Define the programming thesis, roadmap, budget, KPI model, and operating cadence for a Space whose job is to make Shopify unmistakably useful and culturally relevant for London entrepreneurs, retailers, creators, and commerce communities.
* **Make the case for why Spaces matter.** Turn the London Space into a strategic asset for Shopify: a place where entrepreneurs get more successful, our role in retail and commerce becomes tangible, and the brand earns attention because the work is useful, surprising, and worth sharing.
* **Build the system, not just the calendar.** Establish how ideas are sourced, briefed, greenlit, produced, marketed, measured, and, when they are not strong enough, killed.
* **Act as curator-in-chief.** Be the gatekeeper for only “hell yes” opportunities. Program a mix of pop-ups, founder salons, product education, retail experiments, community dinners, workshops, talks, launches, and cultural moments that feel inevitable, not busy.
* **Make London feel like London.** Stay close to the founders, retailers, creatives, agencies, communities, neighbourhoods, and brands shaping commerce in the city. Spot the people worth backing before they are obvious.
* **Produce moments people repeat.** Own the end-to-end experience with your team, including the tiny details people remember without knowing why. The work should be strong enough in the room and interesting enough to travel on social afterwards.
* **Use the product, not just the logo.** Make Shopify’s commerce platform visible in retail experiments and pop-up infrastructure, from Point of Sale to Shop App moments like geo-gated drops, merchant storytelling, inventory, payments, and checkout.
* **Build the team.** Hire, manage, and develop the soon-to-be-built London Spaces team, including senior event producers, event operations, and partnership marketing roles.
* **Own the partner and vendor ecosystem.** Establish and manage relationships with experiential agencies, freelancers, fabricators, AV teams, caterers, staffing partners, security, and local collaborators who determine whether an idea survives contact with reality.
* **Run the machine.** Own the practical reality of a permanent Space, including budgets, security, storage, AV, maintenance, rituals, and operating standards that keep the Space sharp every day.
* **Measure what actually matters.** Attendance, qualified community growth, pipeline influence, product engagement, partner value, and earned attention all matter. So do the harder-to-measure moments that make people feel inspired, connected, and more likely to build with Shopify.
# What we’re looking for
* **Founder-grade experiential judgement.** You have built events, spaces, festivals, pop-ups, communities, or cultural programs where the stakes were real and the details mattered. You know because you have done it, not because you supervised from a distance.
* **Taste, demonstrably.** A body of work you can point to, defend, and critique honestly.
* **Cultural fluency in London.** You know when to show up and when to sit out. You understand where entrepreneurs, retailers, creators, and communities actually gather, not just where trend reports say they do.
* **Production fluency.** Credibility with the vendors and partners who make the work real. You can speak confidently with fabricators, AV teams, caterers, staffing partners, agencies, security, and landlords.
* **Systems thinking.** You can hold a three-year ambition and a broken microphone in the same afternoon. You build the process that lets creative work scale without sanding off its edge.
* **Senior influence.** You can advise executives and make a case with sharp reasoning rather than consensus theatre.
* **Operational nerve.** You are calm inside complexity and can make order out of chaos.
* **Curious about commerce and technology.** You do not need to be a Shopify expert on day one. You do need to care about entrepreneurs, retail, culture, and the pace of change in commerce.
This role probably is not for you if your strongest work is executing someone else’s event brief inside an established machine. We need someone who can design the operating system for a new Space, set a high creative bar, know which opportunities deserve a hard no, and still break the pattern when the right idea comes along.
# Practical details
* This is a hybrid London-based role. Expect to spend more time on site in year one while building out the strategy, operating rhythm, and team.
* At full operation, expect to work from the London Space approximately three days a week, with flexibility around major activations.
* Some programming will happen at night or on weekends. This is part of the role.
* Occasional travel may be required.
# How to apply
No cover letters. Send a CV or portfolio link if it helps us understand your work. In the application below, we're going to ask these two questions. These questions are about taste, cultural understanding, and how you see London.
1. **Who would make the line go around the block?** Name one relatively unheard-of London-based brand, business, creator, founder, community, or shop you would partner with for the Space. What would you build with them, who would come, and why should Shopify be the one to host it?
2. **Where do London entrepreneurs actually hang out?** We’re new to London. Give us a short map, list, voice note, deck, or memo of the physical places, rooms, shops, studios, communities, and neighbourhoods we should understand before opening. Tell us the five you would visit first and why.
## About Shopify
Opportunity is not evenly distributed. Shopify puts independence within reach for anyone with a dream to start a business. We propel entrepreneurs and enterprises to scale the heights of their potential. Since 2006, we’ve grown to over 8,300 employees and generated over $1 trillion in sales for millions of merchants in 175 countries.
This is life-defining work that directly impacts people’s lives as much as it transforms your own. This is putting the power of the few in the hands of the many, is a future with more voices rather than fewer, and is creating more choices instead of an elite option.
## About you
Moving at our pace brings a lot of change, complexity, and ambiguity—and a little bit of chaos. Shopifolk thrive on that and are comfortable being uncomfortable. That means Shopify is not the right place for everyone.
Before you apply, consider if you can:
* Care deeply about what you do and about making commerce better for everyone
* Excel by seeking professional and personal hypergrowth
* Keep up with an unrelenting pace (the week, not the quarter)
* Be resilient and resourceful in face of ambiguity and thrive on (rather than endure) change
* Bring critical thought and opinion
* Put AI agents and tools to work on the tasks they're built for, and focus on the work only humans can do
* Embrace differences and disagreement to get shit done and move forward
* Work digital-first for your daily work
*We may use AI-enabled tools to screen, select, and assess applications. All AI outputs are reviewed and validated by our recruitment team.*

About Simply Blue Energy:
Founded in 2011 under the brand Simply Blue Group in, Simply Blue Energy (SBE) was formally established in 2025 to recognise Kansai Electric Power Co., Inc.’s (“KEPCO”) Share Subscription Agreement with Simply Blue Energy (OSW) Ltd, the offshore wind division of Simply Blue Group.
Simply Blue Energy is an ambitious, values-driven company at the forefront of the global blue economy and is actively developing a significant offshore wind portfolio comprising of 8 GW of floating offshore wind and 4 GW of fixed-bottom wind projects across multiple markets.
Our offshore wind portfolio includes Erebus, a 100MW test and demonstration project, which was awarded a Contract for Difference (CfD) in 2026, and the Salamander project in Scotland. The portfolio also comprises Emerald, Western Star and Aird Mhòr na Mara in Ireland, as well as projects in Spain and Portugal developed under the IberBlue Wind platform. To find out more about us, please visit www.simplyblueenergy.com
About Erebus by Blue Gem Wind:
Erebus is a world leading 100 MW test and demonstration floating offshore wind project located off the coast of Pembroke and is being developed by Simply Blue Energy’s Blue Gem Wind project company. Erebus was awarded a CfD in Allocation Round 7 and as a fully consented project now enters late-stage development, targeting a COD in 2030. The project is progressing through project finance structuring towards Financial Close.
While focused on Erebus, the postholder is part of the SBE Project Excellence Solutions (PES) team and may occasionally support PES activities to maintain alignment across functions.
Key Responsibilities
CDM Principal Designer duties
Coordinate pre-construction H&S across all Erebus design packages, Pre-FEED to construction, per CDM 2015.
Work with the Design Risk Manager to eliminate/reduce hazards in design decisions (floating structure, mooring, cabling, substation, installation/access).
Maintain the design risk register, DRAs, ALARP register; compile PCI and Health and Safety File at each gateway.
Coordinate H&S input across designers, close out interface hazards, prepare F10 notification.
Health & Safety Director duties
Establish and lead the project HSMS (ISO 45001, G9/GWO) across in-house contractor packages, developing the Execution Phase H&S Plan.
Set and audit contractor HSMS compliance; lead pre-qualification/tender reviews and HAZOP/HAZID workshops.
Own H&S strategy and policy; chair governance and incident/near-miss reviews.
Liaise with the Independent Verification Body and HSE; report to SBE H&S Director and Blue Gem Wind Board.
Marine, regulatory and interface responsibilities
Lead marine operations planning and MWS liaison; support consenting/lease obligations; provide H&S evidence for Lender's due diligence and FID sign-off.
Coordinate H&S interfaces across contracted packages with the Process Safety Engineer on major accident hazards.
Health & Safety PES Excellence
Improve H&S tools, templates and guidance; update Simply Blueprint.
Join PES workshops/Chinwags and team meetings; share lessons learned and progress reports.
Interface with other PES/SBE functions.
Track legislation and best practice; keep Simply Blueprint current.
Support fundraising/shareholder transactions with due diligence input.
Experience and Qualifications:
Required:
10 years' relevant experience in health & safety in construction or engineering.
At least 5 years’ experience in the offshore wind sector, including at least 3 years’ senior health & safety leadership experience.
At least 5 years’ demonstrable experience acting as Principal Designer and/or leading health & safety on at least one major project, ideally through to Final Investment Decision (FID), in offshore wind, renewables or large-scale infrastructure.
Strong, hands-on health & safety and design risk management experience — hazard identification, risk assessment and control, and change management on complex, multi-contractor capital projects.
Proven experience building and managing a health & safety team, including direct line management responsibility.
Strong working knowledge of CDM 2015, design risk management processes and health & safety management systems for large capital projects.
Ability to communicate health & safety performance and risk status clearly and credibly to senior stakeholders, including boards, sponsors and lenders.
Excellent organisation skills with the ability to manage own workload, meet timescales and coordinate a number of external and internal stakeholders.
Excellent communication skills, with the ability to enable effective discussion and transfer of information between design team, team members and other stakeholders.
Ability to work as a member of a large, multidisciplinary and international team.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office, with the ability to use relevant applications effectively to support analysis, reporting and senior-level communication.
Ability to create and communicate complex technical information clearly.
Desired:
Relevant degree in engineering, construction, health & safety, or a related discipline.
At least 3 years’ experience of offshore wind project development in the UK.
The technical skills to understand complex offshore operations and the ability to exchange with and understand subject experts.

# Senior Data Analyst – Labour & Productivity (Contractor)
**Department:** Digital & IT
Apply
**The Role..**
We are starting a labour optimisation programme with our Operations team, alongside FP&A and Data Science. The aim is to improve our wage percentage to sales while improving service standards at the same time. We are not interested in an approach that delivers one at the expense of the other.
We are currently selecting an advanced scheduling platform to support this. The analytical foundation underneath it — how we measure productivity, what our labour standards are, how good our demand forecasts need to be — is what this role owns.
You will sit in the Data team and work in close partnership with FP&A. Analysis alone will not move the number; changes stick when a Finance Business Partner and a General Manager can see the opportunity in their own House, agree the size of it and hold it in their forecast. Your job is to give them that, in a form they can act on.
**Key responsibilities..**
* Labour productivity analysis, identifying site-by-site opportunities for efficiency gains and sizing each one
* Work with Operations and Finance to trial changes to scheduling and measure their impact
* Build improved labour reporting, so Business Partners and GMs can see productivity, schedule changes and shift adherence on a daily and weekly cadence
* Support Finance translate demand forecasts into labour requirements, helping to build the models that turn covers, check-ins, treatments and occupancy into hours by role
* Partner with our Data Science and Operations teams to understand forecast accuracy and recommend improvements
* Connect labour deployment to member experience, so that productivity gains are demonstrably not coming out of the House
Required skills and experience
* **Proven experience in labour optimisation.** You have personally delivered measurable improvement in wage percentage or sales per labour hour in a multi-site operation, and can talk us through the levers you pulled, how you sized them and how you proved the result
* A track record of partnering finance and operational stakeholders to land change, not just report on it
* 5+ years in an analytics role, with genuine multi-site operational exposure — hospitality, retail, leisure or QSR
* Advanced SQL, and comfort in a modelled data warehouse (Snowflake and dbt an advantage)
* Strong financial modelling in Excel, and fluency in P&L mechanics — wage percentage, flow-through, contribution
* BI development experience (Omni, Looker, Tableau or Power BI), building tools operators actually use
* Experience with rota, time and attendance and payroll data, and a realistic view of its challenges
* Able to evaluate a demand forecast critically — accuracy, bias, seasonality — without needing to build one
**Desirable**
* Experience with a workforce management or scheduling platform — Unifocus, HotSchedules, Dayforce, Fourth, S4 Labour, UKG, Quinyx or similar

* Labour standards or time-and-motion experience
* Python for analysis, or use of AI tooling such as Claude Code to accelerate it
* Experience linking labour deployment to customer experience outcomes

## **Job Description**
**Are you looking for your next opportunity?**
Sompo has a unique opportunity for an **AVP, Senior Underwriter** in the **Middle Market London team.**
Our Middle Market Underwriting team offers comprehensive multi-line capabilities targeted at select industry verticals of real estate, hospitality, financial institutions, professional services, technology, and life science. We work through a network of retail brokers who share our commitment to long-term partnerships built on a strong service proposition.
This role will focus specifically on the London Property and Casualty team, building our book and working alongside the Head of London for UK Middle Market, and working with our partner brokers in the UK.
Location: This position will be based out of our **London** office. We strive for collaboration which is why we offer a work environment where our employees thrive and develop long lasting careers.
**Our business, your impact, our opportunity:**
**What you’ll be doing:**
* Prioritization and evaluation of new and renewal submissions to identify those accounts that provide the greatest opportunity for profit consistent with the business plan and corporate profit objectives.
* Price and analyze coverage, structure and exposures on individual risks.
* Set appropriate terms and conditions per the Company underwriting strategy and guidelines to quote qualified risks.
* Attend client/broker meetings, lunches, dinners and other social outings as applicable.
* Exercise proper underwriting pricing and discipline to meet profitability goals, complying with underwriting guidelines, systems and procedures.
* Expand existing portfolio of business by developing existing relationships and new prospective clients.
* Support our focus on building strong customer relationships balanced with a strong risk mitigating and compliance-driven culture. Emphasis on proactive monitoring, governance, risk identification and escalation, as well as making sound risk decisions commensurate with the business unit’s risk appetite. Conducts individual account underwriting audits as needed.
* Complete underwriting referral applications for risks outside of your authority for higher level approval as necessary.
* Support the Head of Middle Market London with the development of the underwriting team through referrals and training sessions.
* Support the Middle Market drive to improve operational and underwriting efficiency through project involvement.
**What you’ll bring:**
* Undergraduate, Insurance or advanced degree preferred.
* At least 8+ years of commercial underwriting experience.
* Significant experience within the middle market space.
* Established relationships with retail producers.
* Strong negotiation skills.
* Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word and PowerPoint).
* Excellent communication (both written and verbal) skills.

OverviewApplication
**About Sona**
Frontline work keeps the world running. Restaurants, hospitals, schools, nurseries, airlines, stores, emergency services. Together they employ 80% of the global workforce, over 3 billion people, and they're among the hardest businesses anywhere to run. By-the-minute scheduling, HR and payroll make them far more operationally complex than the average office, yet just 1% of venture funding has ever gone to software built for them.
Rising costs, wage increases, labour shortages and tighter regulation have made fixing that urgent. Sona is the AI-native workforce management platform for frontline organisations, with agents that match staffing to real demand and take the admin load off managers. That's a $500bn+ market the software industry has mostly walked past.
We've raised over $100M from N47, Felicis, Gradient and Northzone, signed more than 100 enterprise customers across the UK and US, and opened offices in London, New York, Austin and Lisbon. More on working at Sona here (https://www.sona.ai/careers).
**About the Role:**
The Director of Support and Services is responsible for building and scaling an AI-first support function. This is a hands-on leadership role combining agent architecture, operational design, product collaboration, and team leadership to solve support at scale without scaling headcount at the same rate.
The role owns the support operating model end to end, defining what agents solve, when they escalate, how they improve, and how humans supervise them. You'll work closely with Product, ML, and Engineering to architect agent behaviour, identify the systemic friction agents miss, and continuously raise agent capability. You'll also lead a lean team focused on configuration, quality monitoring, and exception handling, rather than on taking tickets directly.
Success looks agentic: resolution rates, accuracy, cost per resolution, and how much human time the agents save. If you built a traditional, high-performing support team here, we'd consider that a miss. The aim is support infrastructure where agents are the production layer and humans orchestrate them.
**Responsibilities:**
* Design and own the agentic support operating model, defining what problems agents solve end to end, which require escalation, at what thresholds, and what triggers human review. Own the configuration layer that lets you evolve agent behaviour without shipping code.
* Architect multi-tier agent routing and escalation logic, matching agent assignments to customer segment (self-service, assisted, premium, white-glove) to maximise agent resolution while maintaining quality thresholds.
* Own the cost model around agent operation, human supervision overhead, and escalation. Use agent data to decide when to invest further in agent capability and when to escalate to humans instead.
* Own agent quality and capability metrics, establishing KPIs that track resolution rates, accuracy, customer satisfaction, and human exception workload. Run regular retrospectives on agent failures to identify systematic fixes.
* Work closely with Product and ML to improve agent behaviour, identify friction points agents miss or mishandle, and make the commercial case for whether to train the agent, escalate, or fix the product. Prototype new agent capabilities and guide their build.
* Direct a dedicated engineering resource to build agent infrastructure, including orchestration logic, intelligent routing, multi-turn resolution agents, predictive issue detection, and self-service expansions. You define what agent behaviours to build. They build the plumbing.
* Build and lead a lean, high-performing orchestration team, small by traditional support standards, that owns agent configuration, quality monitoring, exception handling, and continuous improvement. The focus is systemic improvement, not heroic individual performance.
* Define tiered support and services models based on customer segment and agent capability, and define white-glove or premium services where human expertise is the differentiator.
**Requirements:**
* 7+ years in customer support, customer success, or operations roles, including at least 2 years in a leadership capacity. You've operated at scale and understand support economics.
* Hands-on experience building or scaling AI-first workflows where AI is the production layer. You've defined what an AI system should do, found its failure modes, and iterated on its behaviour yourself, rather than just evaluating vendor solutions.
* Deep familiarity with agentic systems and LLM behaviour. You understand agent limitations, failure modes, and hallucination risks, and how to structure problems so agents succeed. You can read traces, identify where agents are going wrong, and communicate fixes to engineers.
* A track record of solving problems systematically through configuration and process design, not by scaling headcount. You've built tiered models, designed escalation logic, and found ways to multiply your team's impact without adding headcount.
* Able to reason about trade-offs in agent design. You understand the tension between agent autonomy (speed, scale) and human oversight (quality, safety), and can make the commercial case for where to draw those lines.
* Comfortable identifying friction and building solutions. You don't wait for process to exist. You move in ambiguity and iterate rapidly.
* Bonus: experience in SaaS, a background in product, engineering, or data, experience building observability or quality frameworks for AI/ML systems, large-scale customer operations or contact centre modernisation experience, or prior experience with agent orchestration platforms.
**Benefits:**

* Extra day of leave for every year of service
* Pension contributions matched up to 5%

* Enhanced parental leave & pay
* Salary sacrifice childcare scheme (Workplace Nursery)
* Annual all expenses paid team retreats
* The latest Macbook and equipment budget for your home office
* Professional development budget
* Unlimited free books

* Supporting and implementing the vision, strategy and values of the business.

job_description:
Who we are
Spectro Cloud is the AI and Kubernetes infrastructure platform behind some of the most demanding environments in the world. Our platform lets enterprises manage the full infrastructure stack, from bare metal to production AI, across data centers, clouds, edge, and air-gapped environments, at fleet scale: some of our customers run thousands of clusters with a handful of engineers.
About the role
Kubernetes is becoming the common infrastructure abstraction under three classes of workloads: VMs, containers, and AI. Multi-cluster management is where that abstraction becomes real, and it's the foundation the rest of our platform stands on. Enterprises come to us with heterogeneous estates: public cloud and managed Kubernetes (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, EKS, AKS, GKE, etc.), on-prem (vSphere, Nutanix, bare metal), all built on Cluster API, some created with our platform, others built outside it. Your job is to make every one of them a first-class citizen: declared, reconciled, and operated with the same rigor regardless of substrate, with no snowflakes.
You will own one of the most established product areas in the company, with a large enterprise and public sector customer base, and drive its next chapter: making multi-cluster infrastructure the substrate that AI workloads run on, adopting clusters built outside our platform as first-class citizens, keeping pace with upstream Kubernetes and Cluster API, and turning long-term support into a product enterprises can buy.
This is a deep domain role. You'll work daily with senior engineering leads and large enterprise customers. It rewards technical fluency and judgment about what not to build.
What you will own
Infrastructure for AI workloads: bare metal and private cloud as the high-performance substrate for GPU clusters, in partnership with our AI product area. Multi-cluster is where AI factories actually run.
Cluster lifecycle across every substrate: provisioning, upgrades, scaling, and Day-2 operations for clusters on public clouds, private clouds, and bare metal, including the customer-facing side of platform transitions: when the ecosystem moves and clusters must follow, you own the migration experience and its communication. You own the "why and what"; engineering owns the how.
Brownfield adoption and federation: the strategic direction of the area. Take clusters built outside our platform from read-only visibility to fully managed, without disruption. This is what wins large enterprise estates.
Long-term support as a product: LTS for Kubernetes versions and workloads, vendor relationships that back it, and the version support policy customers plan against. This area has direct revenue attached.
Estate organization and multi-tenancy: how enterprises carve up large cluster estates with tenant and team boundaries, shared versus dedicated clusters, bringing existing clusters under management, and the access and isolation model that makes one platform safe for many teams.
This map will evolve. The portfolio is growing faster than the org chart, and PMs here regularly take ownership of new product areas as they emerge, including products not yet announced. Expect your scope to expand as the platform does, deliberately and in dialogue with you.
How you will work
Evidence over opinion: usage telemetry and customer signals over the loudest voice, including your own.
Commitments are commitments: this area ships on release trains with enterprise customers planning around dates. Refined epics, explicit scope, honest slip communication.
One org: PM, UX, and Docs operate as a single group; you bring design and documentation in at the definition stage.
AI-native by default: we expect every PM to multiply their output with AI tooling, daily.
Remote-first across US, EU, and India time zones. Clear async writing is how decisions happen here.
Minimum Qualifications
We don't expect the ideal candidate to check every box. The items below are what we look for; don't let a gap discourage you from applying.
5+ years of product management on infrastructure products, with hands-on exposure to 2 or more platform families: ideally one public cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP, or their managed Kubernetes services) and one on-prem (vSphere, Nutanix, bare metal).
Real Kubernetes depth: you understand cluster lifecycle, upgrades, and operators well enough to earn the respect of senior engineers and enterprise platform teams. Cluster API familiarity is a strong plus.
Judgment about maturity: this area includes fast-moving strategic work and stable surfaces that need discipline more than features. You can tell which is which and invest accordingly.
Comfort with upstream ecosystems: you understand what tracking upstream Kubernetes costs and buys. Participation in CNCF SIGs, working groups, or open source communities is a plus, not a bar.
Clear written communication across time zones and cultures.
CKA/CKAD or similar hands-on Kubernetes certification is a nice signal, never a requirement.
The hiring process
Your time is valuable, so the process is short and each stage has a purpose:
Screening interview (30 min): mutual fit and a walk through your experience.
Product interview (60 min): a working session on a real problem from this domain. We're looking at how you think, scope, and decide.
Technical depth interview (45 min): Kubernetes and infrastructure fluency, with one of our senior engineering leads.
Culture and team interview (30 min): working in a team setting, alignment with our core values.
Why this role
Foundation product area with a loyal enterprise and public sector base, and a clear strategic direction into brownfield federation and AI infrastructure.
Small senior team, direct access to founders, engineering leadership, and customers.
Real ownership: this domain has one PM, and it's you.

job_description:
Six-month contract, full time, Remote within European time zones.
While generic AI struggles with hallucinations and shallow analysis, Fortune 500 brands need strategic intelligence they can trust with billion-dollar decisions. We're building the specialized AI that delivers it.
We are Stravito and this is the problem we solve.
Stravito transforms how Consumer Insights professionals and Brand Managers work by building AI that automates their core workflows while eliminating hallucinations. We help world-leading organizations across industries accelerate strategic decision-making by turning millions of market research documents into intelligent systems that generate reports, discover insights proactively, and synthesize knowledge across vast content libraries.
The Mission
Design plays a central role in how we build and talk about Stravito. You'll take our public website from where it is now to where it should be. You'll design and build the pages that matter most, tighten the theme everything runs on, and leave behind a site the next person can pick up and understand. Both halves of the work, done by one person, with no handover in the middle.
Who you'll work with
You'll work closely with our marketing team. They decide what the website needs to say. What we build in the product, and how we position it, reaches the website through them, and it moves fast. A lot of the work is campaign and landing pages for paid traffic, where every page has a clear job and someone is checking whether it does it.
You won't do this alone. Our Creative Director sets the art direction and creates the unique pieces when a page needs more than the system offers. Our Visual Designer makes campaign and content assets. An engineer is there for the heavy technical work. But the website is yours to drive, and the decisions about how it looks and how it's built are yours.
What you'll do
Design and build pages, campaign landing pages and new sections of stravito.com, from first sketch to live.
Turn positioning and campaign briefs into pages that work.
Build the modules that campaign and landing pages are made from, so marketing can move without waiting for you. Care about whether those pages convert.
Work in our HubSpot theme: templates, modules, the local build setup, and the discipline that keeps it tidy.
Write clean, hand-written HTML, CSS and JavaScript when the design needs more than the tools offer.
Keep the site fast, accessible and consistent. Treat performance and accessibility as design problems, not as someone else's checklist.
Document what you build and hand over a site someone else can run. This is part of the job from day one, not something for the last week.
Bring in the Creative Director and Visual Designer when a page needs art direction or new content, and run the rest on your own.
About you
You design and you code. You have several years of experience where you did the visual design and wrote the code that went live, on the same sites.
You have strong visual and typographic judgement. You can explain a layout decision without pointing at a mood board.
You're fluent in HTML and CSS, including modern layout, and comfortable enough with JavaScript to build the interactions you design.
You're comfortable in React, or close enough to be productive in a React codebase within a couple of weeks. HubSpot and HubL experience is a plus, not a must.
You know when to ask for help. An engineer is available for the hard technical parts, and people who use that support well move much faster than people who struggle alone.
You're happy to work from someone else's brief. Marketing decides what the site says. You decide how it looks and how it's built, with art direction from our Creative Director when a page needs it. If you need to own the message too, this isn't the right fit.
You build landing pages fast without leaving a mess. You use reusable modules where it makes sense and one-offs where speed matters, and you know the difference.
Reliable, able to self manage and keep people updated without being chased.
You use AI in your work.
Nice to have
Motion and interaction design, in code or in After Effects.
Experience with marketing websites for B2B software.
A personal website you built yourself and still like.
The practical details
Six-month contract, full time.
This is a contractor position. Fully remote. You need to be based within two hours of Central European Time.
How to apply
The application form asks you to share two or three live sites and to tell us, for each one, what you designed and what you coded yourself. Please be specific. We look forward to hearing from you!

Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies, from the world’s largest enterprises to ambitious startups, use Stripe to accept payments, manage their businesses, and grow their revenue. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a significant amount of work ahead. You’ll have an opportunity to help put the global economy within everyone’s reach. About the team
The Foreign Exchange team builds the products and infrastructure that help Stripe users operate across currencies. Businesses increasingly operate globally from the moment they launch, collecting revenue, holding balances, paying suppliers, and managing expenses across multiple currencies.
Managing those currencies remains fragmented. Finance teams must decide what to hold, when to convert, how to manage currency exposure, and how to reconcile the results. Today, these workflows often span banks, spreadsheets, treasury systems, and specialist FX providers.
Stripe is uniquely positioned to simplify this. We sit at the center of the payments, Billing, balances, payouts, and settlement flows that create a business’s currency needs. Our vision is to make Stripe the financial home for businesses operating internationally, with a unified offering for holding, converting, and managing currencies and FX risk.
A core part of this vision is making currency management agentic. We believe software agents will increasingly help businesses understand their FX position, recommend actions, and manage currencies within defined policies and controls.
This could include Stripe-native agents that monitor exposure and take approved actions. It could also mean enabling customers’ own agents to use Stripe’s infrastructure to understand balances and exposures, obtain pricing, execute conversions or hedges, and reconcile the results.
Our goal is to make Stripe the currency-management layer that both people and agents can build on.
We will build these capabilities both for globally operating businesses and for the platforms and marketplaces that use Connect.
What you’ll do
We’re looking for a Product Manager to build a new area of Stripe’s FX and currency-management offering. This is a zero-to-one product role at the intersection of FX, treasury, and agentic AI. You will help define what agentic currency management should look like. That could mean Stripe-native agents that understand exposure, recommend actions, and execute within customer-defined policies. It could also mean enabling customers’ own agents to use Stripe’s FX infrastructure to understand balances, obtain pricing, manage risk, execute transactions, and reconcile the results.
You will work directly with globally operating businesses to understand their most important currency-management problems. You will identify the right initial product wedge and take it from discovery through launch and iteration. Today, treasury teams assemble exposures from multiple systems, determine hedge requirements, monitor changing positions, request pricing, execute trades, and reconcile the results. We believe much of this workflow can become continuous, intelligent, and increasingly automated.
You might build products that combine Stripe’s real-time view of payments, balances, and settlement activity with customer forecasts and policies to identify exposures and recommend actions. You might also define the APIs, permissions, controls, and financial primitives that allow customer or third-party agents to safely take those actions through Stripe.
Over time, these systems could move from surfacing insights to requesting quotes, executing conversions or hedges, rebalancing positions, and escalating exceptions within clearly defined permissions.
You will determine which intelligence Stripe should provide directly, which capabilities we should expose for others to build on, where humans should remain in the decision loop, and how we evaluate whether agents are making good decisions. Your product area could also include automated conversion and balance policies, recurring currency-management workflows, or capabilities distributed through Connect.
